item.title: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona
item.description: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona Joao Cancelo has emerged as one of Alejandro Balde’s strongest supporters within the Barcelona dressing room, offering encouragement and advice as the defender struggles to establish himself under Hansi Flick. According to Mundo Deportivo , the Portuguese full-back has even defended his teammate in conversations with the German manager, while showing concern among senior players over Balde’s situation. The development comes amid uncertainty surrounding Balde’s Barcelona future. As previously reported, the academy graduate is increasingly open to leaving in January after struggling to secure regular playing time. In fact, despite Barcelona’s defensive injury problems, he has managed just 116 minutes across four appearances, raising questions about his standing in Flick’s plans. Cancelo takes Alejandro Balde under his wing Cancelo has emerged as Balde’s biggest supporter. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Cancelo’s support is, in fact, an interesting development given Balde’s initial reaction to his arrival at Barcelona. As per the outlet, the Spaniard struggled to understand the decision to sign another left-back, particularly as he was expected to be Flick’s first choice. As it turns out, however, their relationship has evolved, with the experienced Portuguese defender now regularly encouraging Balde, offering advice and reassuring him during a difficult period. It has even been suggested that Cancelo has also spoken to Flick in his teammate’s defence on at least one occasion. Another Barcelona senior player questions Flick As per the outlet, Cancelo is not the only senior figure concerned about how Flick has handled Balde, as another influential Barcelona player, who enjoys direct communication with the manager, also questioned one of his training decisions. Balde is likely to leave Barcelona in January. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The incident involved Flick changing Balde’s position during a training match. The teammate reportedly challenged the decision, questioning how the defender could demonstrate his abilities when he was not being trained in his natural position. What happens now? Notably, the situation adds to Balde’s increasingly difficult relationship with his role at Barcelona. Having spent most of his development at the club since joining the academy, he is now facing uncertainty over his long-term prospects. Now, with January approaching, the support of senior dressing-room figures could prove important, although unless his opportunities improve, Balde may still consider leaving to secure the regular football he wants.

item.title: 🗞️ Madrid flying high; Barça joy, Monday’s front pages
item.description: 🗞️ Madrid flying high; Barça joy, Monday’s front pages A new week kicks off with plenty of fixtures on the horizon. The first arrive this Tuesday: another round of Champions League action with plenty at stake and Spanish teams badly needing to keep picking up points. Meanwhile, Real Madrid claimed another convincing win over Racing Santander yesterday. Goals from Diomandé, Mbappé and Bellingham highlighted a match that underlined the fine form of José Mourinho's side. In Barcelona, spirits remain high after the thrashing of Alavés. A positive mood to start a week packed with headlines on the newsstands. Here are the front pages for today, Monday, November 2. item.title: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany
item.description: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ): Ex-Borussia Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela is confident Jürgen Klopp is the right man who can restore the German national team to it's former glory. “He is able to change the important things in a short matter of time, and that’s what makes him a good fit," Owomoyela said at a media round in Munich attended by Bulinews.com . “I wish he could have the Germany guys every day [to practice] but that’s not the case. As I said, he’s able to create an instant impact and a clear vision of what to do. “Now more than before, his reputation helps players believe what he is saying. All of that is a good fit for a coach with less time but can make things happen. “It’s just about finding the right people. He used a lot of players [in his first international period] and that will be the case going forward too," the Hamburg native added. Having played under Klopp at Dortmund for five seasons between 2008 and 2013, Owomoyela gave some fascinating insights into what the 59-year-old demands from his squad. “He was a coach who pushed for hard work but have fun while doing it. He always had fun it seemed, Even though he asked a lot of us, he would let us have fun as well. “He was the loudest in the dressing rooms, so he gave you that kind of freedom. But, you had to back it up on the pitch working hard and doing what he asked. “He could create pictures. He made it really easy to understands where he wanted you to go and what he wanted you to do. It was like a movie in your head. “So, that kind of ability to get you motivated to do what you need to do, it’s what puts him above many others. He wanted us to play the most intense football. "It was hunt, hunt, hunt, always hunt. If you got the ball, run fast at your opponent as hard as possible. If they [the opponent] got the ball, go hunt it [back] again. "He would play games too, if we ran 120 kilometres [as a team] one week, next week he would say let’s do 124 [kilometres]. We believed in what he was saying. “Even though we lost games and derbies, he would say it doesn’t matter because he felt we were going in the right direction,” he said, speaking with a undeniable passion. Perhaps the proof is in the pudding. During his time at a once lowly BVB side, he transformed them into a deadly force which claimed two Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal. Whether that can be replicated on the international stage is up for debate. However, in Owomoyela's mind, Klopp possesses the necessary traits to bring dreams into reality.

item.title: 'Absolutely embarrassing!' - Gary Neville slams Arsenal star Gabriel for 'play-acting' during Premier League victory over Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville has strongly criticised Arsenal defender Gabriel for his embarrassing play-acting during a vital Premier League victory over Liverpool at Anfield. The Brazilian went down clutching his face following a minor collision, prompting a fierce response from the former Manchester United captain on commentary. Gabriel criticised for Anfield theatrics Neville has accused Gabriel of embarrassing play-acting during Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool . Mikel Arteta's side secured a vital 1-0 win at Anfield to move three points clear at the top of the table. The controversy occurred in the opening minutes of the tense encounter following a physical collision between the Brazilian defender and Liverpool striker Alexander Isak. Gabriel immediately went down holding his face and appealed to referee Andy Madley for a foul. However, television replays quickly exposed the true nature of the incident involving the Arsenal centre-back. The footage clearly showed that Isak's arm had only made contact with Gabriel's upper chest rather than his face. Neville tears into the defender Neville was far from impressed with the theatrical reaction and voiced his frustration on Sky Sports commentary. The former United defender believes Gabriel must permanently remove this behaviour from his game. "He does let himself down at times," Neville stated. "I love his fire, his passion and his tenacity. But there’s a push into his upper chest and he goes down holding his face." Neville continued his assessment with a blunt final verdict on the Anfield incident. He added: "It’s absolutely embarrassing. He needs to stop doing that." Arsenal secure a massive away victory Despite the early controversy, Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game after 16 minutes to seal all three points. The narrow defeat was a bitter blow for Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, who remain fifth in the table and outside the Champions League places. Neville was quick to praise Arsenal for their resilience and tactical discipline following the final whistle. He highlighted the sheer magnitude of securing a clean sheet at such a notoriously difficult venue. "It was a defensive masterclass from Arsenal," Neville explained. "Andoni Iraola will be upset, he will feel like his team have given everything, but they put themselves right in the driving seat." European football returns for both clubs Arsenal must quickly shift their focus away from domestic matters as they prepare for a midweek European away trip. Arteta's men travel to the Czech Republic to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League, hoping to extend their excellent run of form. Liverpool also return to Champions League action in the coming days as they desperately look to bounce back from this frustrating league disappointment. Iraola will take his squad to Turkey for a highly challenging fixture against Fenerbahce.

item.title: Iran Warns New War Could Last Longer After Trump Threatens Strikes
item.description: Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. “A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen. Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran. “We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. Trump reiterated his threat on Sunday, telling a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of midterm elections, that he may have to give Tehran “the hammer” at some unspecified time. The warning came after US media reported that Trump had held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over whether and when to ramp up combat operations against the Islamic republic. Axios quoted one US and one Israeli official saying the two leaders discussed the state of negotiations with Iran, with Netanyahu pressing the president to strike the country immediately after Tuesday’s US midterm elections and Trump eager to let negotiations play out. The Israeli source described the call as “tough”, while the US source said it was “direct”, according to Axios. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump confirmed he had discussed Iran with Netanyahu, but would not elaborate. A woman walks past a mural bearing the Iranian national flag in Tehran on October 26, 2026. ‘No Geographical Limitations’ Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. “A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen. Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran. “We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. Trump reiterated his threat on Sunday, telling a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of midterm elections, that he may have to give Tehran “the hammer” at some unspecified time. The warning came after US media reported that Trump had held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over whether and when to ramp up combat operations against the Islamic republic. Axios quoted one US and one Israeli official saying the two leaders discussed the state of negotiations with Iran, with Netanyahu pressing the president to strike the country immediately after Tuesday’s US midterm elections and Trump eager to let negotiations play out. The Israeli source described the call as “tough”, while the US source said it was “direct”, according to Axios. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump confirmed he had discussed Iran with Netanyahu, but would not elaborate. A woman walks past a mural bearing the Iranian national flag in Tehran on October 26, 2026. ‘No Geographical Limitations’ Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack. Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. “In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “We hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy,” adding that Iran “remains prepared for both defence and diplomacy”, according to the official IRNA news agency. The warnings came as Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed on Saturday that he had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance seeking to revive talks. Rezaei noted what he described as a positive change in “tone” from the US side but said he had yet to respond. He said Tehran had previously told Washington that unless its conditions were met, “neither would the Strait of Hormuz be reopened nor would there be any negotiations”. Those conditions include unfreezing Iranian assets abroad, ending the months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports, lifting longstanding sanctions and ending the war on all fronts. Since the war began, Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorisation. The United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports. Participants, including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, attend the leaders’ summit of the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP 17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in the Armenian capital, Yerevan, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by STRINGER / AFP) | STRINGER / AFP ‘Braced For The Worst’ Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president, said on Sunday that the United Arab Emirates hoped the exchanges would yield a breakthrough, but was preparing for the worst. “It is not the interest of the region to go through another round… But I think we’re also, as we’ve shown before, braced for the worst,” he told a conference in Manama. In Tehran, some residents described a sense of helplessness as threats of renewed fighting mount. “The news coming in is truly worrying. However… there is nothing I can actually do about it,” Mohadese, a 27-year-old health inspector, told AFP. Others, including 48-year-old vendor Ebrahim, saw no reason to be concerned. “We do not fear another war; we have been at war for 48 years now — we are always at war,” he said in downtown Tehran. item.title: 'It'll make us dizzy' - Gennaro Gattuso warns Lazio stars not to look at the Serie A table despite going top with comeback win over Cagliari
item.description: SS Lazio v Cagliari Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso has urged his players to ignore the Serie A standings despite moving clear at the summit with a 2-1 comeback win over Cagliari on Sunday. The Italian tactician insists his unbeaten side must remain grounded and prioritise reaching the 40-point mark after claiming a sixth consecutive league victory. Italian boss demands complete focus Gattuso refused to get carried away at the Stadio Olimpico even though the Biancocelesti sit top after 10 games for the first time since 2010-11. Sunday's triumph allowed the hosts to capitalise on Inter losing to AC Milan on Saturday . They have also recorded six straight league wins for the first time since Simone Inzaghi's reign in 2021. Late header seals comeback triumph Having netted 24 goals in their opening 10 fixtures for the first time since 2017-18, the hosts trailed to M'Bala Nzola's 20th-minute opener until Gustav Isaksen equalised in the 36th minute, setting the stage for substitute Andrea Pinamonti to head an 83rd-minute winner. Focusing on the club's 40-point target rather than the standings, Gattuso told DAZN Italia : "We are all up there, we still need 12 points to achieve the target of 40 that we set at the start of the season. "Every team in the league is balanced and well-structured, so we've got to keep taking it one game at a time and see where we end up. It is best that we don't look at the table right now, or it'll make us dizzy. We've got to push hard, rest, then push hard again." Unbeaten leaders show relentless spirit Alongside third-placed Roma, who sit four points behind under Gian Piero Gasperini, the leaders remain unbeaten in Serie A this season. Insisting his side must maintain their determination after responding to an earlier cup setback , Gattuso added: "That defeat didn't take away our belief in what we were doing, we don't let go. We work, we don't complain, this is the spirit that is pushing us on, because without that, we become a normal team." Crediting his substitutes for changing the contest against stubborn visitors, he continued: "It was a very difficult match and all credit for that goes to Cagliari, because we struggled and those who came off the bench changed the game with their mentality. This was a very important match for us, we did everything to take the result home. Cagliari are tough to deal with, they defend and attack well." Napoli test precedes international break Gattuso will now prepare his squad to face an out-of-form Napoli side in their final league match before the November international break. Maintaining their winning momentum will be vital as they seek to protect their cushion at the summit. Meanwhile, Cagliari must regroup quickly after suffering four straight top-flight defeats for the first time since April.

item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Monday, November 2
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Archie Gray of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace FC at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) | Getty Images good morning everyone and welcome to november! The turning of the calendar means it’s time to Take a Look at the Month Ahead, where hoddle HQ checks out the month’s schedule for the men’s and women’s teams at Tottenham Hotspur Football Club. Tottenham Hotspur men’s squad: The boys enter November having won three games on the bounce. The last time they did that was more than 600 days ago. Is the tide beginning to turn? I never like those questions because I follow Tottenham Hotspur, and history cautions me against believing corners have been turned. But this month’s light selection of matches is temping. Oh boy, is it tempting. Still, I’m looking forward to a difficult match against Leeds United on 7th November. Leeds haven’t lost at home since March 3 (that was a 0-1 loss to Sunderland). This season, they’re 1-3-0 at home against mostly decent competition. Form like that is difficult to break down, so I’m quite cautious heading into this weekend. Then there are two matches against a surprisingly steady Ipswich Town and bottom-of-the-pack Sunderland. You might be surprise to learn Town have scored more goals than Spurs this season, although they have a -4 goal differential. Sunderland are looking pretty bad though, which isn’t surprising given the additional football they have to play in Europe. Seven points should be the minimum expectations, but I’ll accept nine points. November schedule: at Leeds (7 Nov); Ipswich Town (21 Nov); at Sunderland (29 Nov) Tottenham Hotspur women’s squad: A little bit of a different form for the ladies. A 4-1 win against Bournemouth on Sunday snapped an ugly three-game skid in league play in which they were outscored 14-4. That shows there’s still a large gap between Spurs and the rest of the league, even if they sit fourth. We’ve got a mixed bag this month. Brighton will be a good test, and I think there are some good opportunities for their League Cup group play before a big test against Manchester City to end the month. November schedule: Brighton (8 Nov); Crystal Place (11 Nov, Women’s League Cup); Everton (14 Nov); Leicester (18 Nov, Women’s League Cup); Man City (22 Nov) Fitzie’s track of the day: II B.S., by Charles Mingus And now for your links: Alasdair Gold : “The huge Luca Williams-Barnett mistake Tottenham can’t make and Van Hecke’s remarkable visitors” The Athletic ($$) : “Are Tottenham, at last, a good team again?” The Telegraph : “Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage” The Independent : “Police investigate fan taunt using Bradley Lowery photo during Coventry vs Sunderland”

item.title: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick
item.description: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick Manchester United fans had to face up to another loss on Saturday afternoon, this time coming against Chelsea. Current situation Michael Carrick’s job appears safe until the next international break, which begins in a week, but he must navigate matches against AS Roma and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. It is widely expected that Carrick will lose his job in the not-too-distant future, with the side sitting seventeenth in the league, above the drop zone on goal difference. There have been numerous names linked to the Old Trafford hot seat, such as Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler. Nonetheless, one name that should also be one hundred percent on the club’s list is Unai Emery. Fabrizio Romano has stated that the club do in fact admire the Spaniard and he would be an incredible choice to replace Carrick. The case for Unai Emery Villa job The job Emery has done at Aston Villa is nothing short of spectacular. In the context of regularly having to sell his best players and failing to replace them with huge names, he continues to get his side firing. They won the Europa League last season and also finished fourth in the league. He has won 116 of his 211 matches at Aston Villa, boasting a win percentage of 55. The Spaniard is also a winner, as he has won five separate Europa Leagues: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and, of course, last season’s with Villa. Tactics What’s more, Emery is a strong tactician who regularly gets the best out of players. Villa lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins this summer, all crucial players to the first eleven. Most managers would crumble or throw their toys out of the pram. Emery’s response: second place in the Champions League with three wins from three. The league has been tougher going as they currently sit ninth, but showed their quality by beating Manchester City 2-1 two weekends ago. Emery has been described as a manager who is “the outstanding current example of the game-plan school: a stable structure underneath, an opponent-specific plan on top, and a depth of preparation that turns information into confidence.” He can be flexible and instructs his team to play with and without the ball with ease. The Spaniard is also famed for his tactical preparation, with “Emery’s weeks being built backwards from the opponent. Video analysis is the spine of preparation, hours of it, with the plan fed to players across the week through unit meetings, individual clips and walkthroughs rather than dumped on them the day before the game.” An itch to scratch at bigger clubs Finally, while it may be hard to see Emery walking away from the success he has built at Villa, he will have an itch to scratch at a truly massive football club. Current situation Michael Carrick’s job appears safe until the next international break, which begins in a week, but he must navigate matches against AS Roma and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. It is widely expected that Carrick will lose his job in the not-too-distant future, with the side sitting seventeenth in the league, above the drop zone on goal difference. There have been numerous names linked to the Old Trafford hot seat, such as Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler. Nonetheless, one name that should also be one hundred percent on the club’s list is Unai Emery. Fabrizio Romano has stated that the club do in fact admire the Spaniard and he would be an incredible choice to replace Carrick. The case for Unai Emery Villa job The job Emery has done at Aston Villa is nothing short of spectacular. In the context of regularly having to sell his best players and failing to replace them with huge names, he continues to get his side firing. They won the Europa League last season and also finished fourth in the league. He has won 116 of his 211 matches at Aston Villa, boasting a win percentage of 55. The Spaniard is also a winner, as he has won five separate Europa Leagues: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and, of course, last season’s with Villa. Tactics What’s more, Emery is a strong tactician who regularly gets the best out of players. Villa lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins this summer, all crucial players to the first eleven. Most managers would crumble or throw their toys out of the pram. Emery’s response: second place in the Champions League with three wins from three. The league has been tougher going as they currently sit ninth, but showed their quality by beating Manchester City 2-1 two weekends ago. Emery has been described as a manager who is “the outstanding current example of the game-plan school: a stable structure underneath, an opponent-specific plan on top, and a depth of preparation that turns information into confidence.” He can be flexible and instructs his team to play with and without the ball with ease. The Spaniard is also famed for his tactical preparation, with “Emery’s weeks being built backwards from the opponent. Video analysis is the spine of preparation, hours of it, with the plan fed to players across the week through unit meetings, individual clips and walkthroughs rather than dumped on them the day before the game.” An itch to scratch at bigger clubs Finally, while it may be hard to see Emery walking away from the success he has built at Villa, he will have an itch to scratch at a truly massive football club. At Paris Saint-Germain, he did win one league, two national cups and two league cups. Nonetheless, as he did not win the Champions League, he was never given the respect he probably deserved in France. What’s more, his time at Arsenal is probably viewed as a failure given he lost the final of the Europa League and did not win a trophy. He could well see the United job as an attempt to finally gain recognition at one of the hottest seats in world football. Final thoughts There is no doubt extracting Emery from Villa could be difficult and expensive. What’s more, his style of football may not always bring United fans to their feet. Nonetheless, his tactical excellence, ability to build coherent teams according to the tools available to him, and his hunger to succeed at a truly giant global name make him an outstanding candidate to turn Manchester United’s sinking ship around. United fans will get another sample of his work this weekend when his Villa side travel to Old Trafford this coming Sunday. Featured image by Carl Recine via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Manager threatened to fire a colleague, then gave them a critical task – which they flubbed
item.description: Welcome to Monday morning, an occasion The Register marks with a new instalment of " Who, Me? " It's our reader-contributed column in which you confess to workplace mistakes and share your escapes from subsequent scrapes. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Gordon" who told us he once worked as an engineer at a major semiconductor corporation. Gordon rose to become manager of an engineering team which worked on a very popular PC chipset. One of the chaps on this team wasn't pulling his weight, so Gordon got the job of telling him to improve, or leave. "In all fairness, he was a nice guy but not a great engineer and needed to be better," Gordon told The Register. Not long after that moment of managerial unpleasantness, Gordon's team got the job of doing a full backup of the chipset's "production stepping" – the silicon equivalent of a minor point release. The idea was to create a detailed record that could be used as a restore point. "This was not a nightly backup, but a purposeful backup to retain a snapshot of the entire cleaned-up design database for future cases where we might need to spin another stepping quickly," Gordon explained. Gordon told his underperforming colleague to do the backup. "Because I was overworked, I did not think this through," he told The Register . The at-risk worker quickly proved why he was under the pump by deciding the backup wasn't necessary until the team completed the next stepping – but didn't tell anyone about that plan. Before that next stepping was done, the employee's past indiscretions caught up with him and he was let go. The story now fast-forwards six years, to a moment when Gordon learned that a customer wanted to buy the old chipset design so they could make a radiation-hardened version to use on satellites. The major semiconductor company liked the sound of that, and asked Gordon to find the backup. "My colleague and I then pieced together what had happened," he wrote. "Being good engineers, we said nothing. We searched through old nightly backup tapes until we found bits and pieces of different steppings of the design database and copied them all to one place, then handed this off to the customer." To this day, Gordon doesn't know if the customer was able to produce a useful chip from the bits of backup he cobbled together. "Did they realize they received bits and pieces of two slightly different databases? Did they care? Was the project canceled before anyone realized it?" "From then on, I was more careful about who I assigned the task of creating restore backups for each design project," he told The Register . "And I kept a record of the emails requesting backups and confirmation that backups had been done." Have you given a job to the wrong person? Or given clients slightly dodgy data? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We would love to tell your tale on a future Monday. ®

item.title: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns
item.description: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams ’ star cornerback Trent McDuffie briefly exited Sunday’s 24-9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers after sustaining a back injury. Head coach Sean McVay did not offer a clear diagnosis following the game; his initial reaction indicated that the team had reasons to remain optimistic about the defender’s condition. While speaking to reporters after the game, based on his initial observations, the Rams head coach offered an encouraging assessment of how the cornerback appeared to be feeling. “He looks like he’s feeling OK,” McVay said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McDuffie went down late in the third quarter after seemingly hurting his back while making a tackle in the backfield. He initially limped off the field and headed to the locker room for further evaluation before eventually making his way back to the sideline. Following the incident, the cornerback was initially listed as questionable to return. However, his appearance on the sideline later in the game offered some encouragement, as he seemed to be doing better after the injury scare. McDuffie had already missed Weeks 6 and 7 after suffering a groin injury during practice. Despite carrying a questionable designation heading into the matchup against the Chargers, he managed to return to action and contribute to the Rams’ defensive effort. Meanwhile, McDuffie was not the only Los Angeles cornerback to suffer an injury during Sunday’s game. Jaylen Watson also left the game in the third quarter with a shoulder issue and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the matchup. Fortunately, the injury setbacks did not prevent the Rams from securing a comfortable victory and extending their winning streak to four games. Meanwhile, the Chargers remained winless after falling to 0-7 this season . The Rams will now have a full week to monitor McDuffie’s recovery before traveling to face the Washington Commanders in Week 9. Related: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers Related: Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers

item.title: Vikings, Chiefs and Cowboys beaten - NFL week eight
item.description: Kyler Murray became Minnesota's starting quarterback after leaving Arizona while Gardner Minshew was signed to be the Cardinals' back-up [Getty Images] The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend. There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime. The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again. Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. NFL's Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury Broncos replace Chiefs in top spot Minnesota put their 6-0 record on the line at their NFC North rivals the Detroit Lions, who won 19-15 to halt the Vikings' unbeaten start. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups. The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24. Patrick Mahomes threw for three touchdowns and 321 yards but that was not enough for the Chiefs as the Broncos' defence made a goal-line stand at the death to clinch victory. The Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) are in charge of the AFC South after romping to a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, who look set for a rebuild. After

Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. NFL's Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury Broncos replace Chiefs in top spot Minnesota put their 6-0 record on the line at their NFC North rivals the Detroit Lions, who won 19-15 to halt the Vikings' unbeaten start. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups. The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24. Patrick Mahomes threw for three touchdowns and 321 yards but that was not enough for the Chiefs as the Broncos' defence made a goal-line stand at the death to clinch victory. The Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) are in charge of the AFC South after romping to a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, who look set for a rebuild. After firing their general manager and trading two key players in the past two weeks, the Colts are reportedly in talks over trading star running back Jonathan Taylor. Meanwhile, the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) beat the Cleveland Browns 26-7 to go top of the AFC North. Burrow firing for Bengals Another of Pittsburgh's divisional rivals, the Cincinnati Bengals, made hard work of it before beating the Tennessee Titans 43-36 in overtime. Despite being intercepted three times by Tennessee's Amani Hooker, Burrow became the first player in 75 years - and only the second ever after Norm van Brocklin's 554 passing yards in a 1951 game - to record more than 450 passing yards, five touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown in a single game. After a mixed start to the season, the former first overall draft pick has also become the first quarterback in NFL history to register a 70% completion percentage plus touchdown passes in three consecutive games. Burrow and his high-powered offence are in ominous form as they seek a Super Bowl return and host Pittsburgh in two weeks. Bucs win without making a pass The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran the ball 56 times while Atlanta had 28 carries for 99 yards [Getty Images] While Cincinnati's offence relies on its passing game and receivers, many of the NFL's running backs grabbed the spotlight on Sunday. For the first time since 2003, at least six players had 140 rushing yards on the same day, including Bucky Irving (170) and Kenneth Gainwell (140) as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0. Torrential rain in Florida made handling conditions difficult so Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes, completing none of them. Instead he spent most of the day handing the ball to Irving or Gainwell as the Bucs racked up a team-record 324 rushing yards. They also became the first team to have zero pass completions since 1974 – and just the second in the Super Bowl era. 'Minshew Magic' stuns Cowboys Tyler Allgeier was the running back who starred for the Arizona Cardinals, rushing for 147 yards at the Dallas Cowboys. But it was eccentric back-up quarterback Gardner Minshew who helped turn the game in Arizona's favour after replacing an ineffective Jacoby Brissett with the Cardinals trailing 17-3 late in the third quarter. After being a late draft pick by Jacksonville in 2019, Minshew has spent most of his career as a back-up and in the off-season Arizona became his sixth team in eight years. He made a thrilling debut, though, becoming the first quarterback this season to throw three touchdown passes in a fourth quarter. That tied the game at the death, and although recent hero Chad Ryland failed to kick the extra point, he redeemed himself in overtime with a field goal to win 33-30. It is only the second time Dallas have ever lost when leading by 10 points inside the final three minutes and leaves them 3-5. It also heaps pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, with outspoken team owner Jerry Jones saying: "It's an indictment of the whole show". item.title: Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
item.description: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have opened up as 2.5-point road underdogs on FanDuel against the New England Patriots in Week 9, coming off a mini-bye after beating the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football . The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he’s posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots’ chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator . Green Bay’s path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. According to The Athletic, the Packers have a 61 percent chance to make the playoffs if they beat the Patriots, but just a 39 percent chance if they lose. If Green Bay can split their trip to New England and their Week 10 game against the Minnesota Vikings, who are sitting in the driver’s seat in the NFC North at the moment, they have about a 50-50 chance of making the playoffs going into their Week 11 bye week. After that, they should be getting some players back from injury lists, notably edge rusher Micah Parsons. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he’s posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots’ chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator . Green Bay’s path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. According to The Athletic, the Packers have a 61 percent chance to make the playoffs if they beat the Patriots, but just a 39 percent chance if they lose. If Green Bay can split their trip to New England and their Week 10 game against the Minnesota Vikings, who are sitting in the driver’s seat in the NFC North at the moment, they have about a 50-50 chance of making the playoffs going into their Week 11 bye week. After that, they should be getting some players back from injury lists, notably edge rusher Micah Parsons. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! Keep Packers coverage and conversation at your fingertips with a faster, easier game-day experience on the SB Nation app. Join Packers fans in our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

item.title: Cardinals’ Gardner Minsew highlights team’s perfect response to Chad Ryland’s FG miss
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Gardner Minsew highlights team’s perfect response to Chad Ryland’s FG miss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals found themselves in the middle of pure gridiron chaos during Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Backup quarterback Gardner Minshew came off the bench in the third quarter for Jacoby Brissett and engineered a thrilling late comeback, connecting with wide receiver Michael Wilson on a 13-yard touchdown pass with just 6 seconds remaining in regulation. However, what should have been a regulation victory turned into overtime drama when kicker Chad Ryland pulled the potential game-winning extra point wide left. Instead of letting the missed kick deflate the sideline, Minshew immediately rallied the locker room with his trademark infectious energy. Speaking with reporters after the game, Minshew broke down how the team quickly wiped the slate clean. “Two or thirty thirty got a chance to go play these boys in overtime, let’s freaking go. You know, sign me up,” Minshew said. “So I think that’s how quick can you reset, how quick can you, cause I think that this is a game that was a total testament to that you know. Forget what happened before, forget everything that’s happened to this point. Just keep going, keep giving yourselves a chance and we had a group of fighters today that was a lot of fun to go with.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Gardner Minshew when asked how he keeps leading the team following Ryland’s missed XP near the end of regulation A very Minshew answer. Great stuff #AZCardinals pic.twitter.com/wfPM5VmN98 — Dom Tibbetts (@DomTibbettsTV) November 1, 2026 Minshew’s unbreakable mindset paid off instantly in the extra frame. After replacing Brissett, the veteran signal-caller put together a masterful performance, completing 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards and 3 touchdowns. Running back Tyler Allgeier added explosive power to the offense, rushing for 147 yards on 11 carries to help Arizona outgain Dallas 467-261. After the Cardinals’ defense forced a punt in overtime, Minshew marched the offense 44 yards downfield. That set up Ryland for a 42-yard field goal attempt, and the kicker split the uprights to redeem himself and lock up a 33-30 victory. Minshew’s poise under pressure proved that no matter how bizarre the circumstances get, Arizona always has a puncher’s chance. Related: Cardinals Mike LaFleur gets real about decision to switch to Gardner Minshew vs. Cowboys Related: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur won’t commit to Gardner Minshew as Week 9 starter despite Cowboys heroics

item.title: Taliban voices 'serious concern' over US plan to deport Afghan migrants via Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban government expressed concern on Monday over reported US plans to deport more than 150 Afghans from the US to Pakistan for an eventual return home, with advocacy groups warning the removal could endanger their lives.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
item.content:encoded: Afghanistan's Taliban government expressed concern on Monday over reported US plans to deport more than 150 Afghans from the US to Pakistan for an eventual return home, with advocacy groups warning the removal could endanger their lives.

item.title: You Should Treat Yourself to a Memorable Destination Birthday in 2027 If You Were Born Between 1977 and 1987
item.description: Generated Image. Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year. Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect. But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended. That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories. So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends: Bali, Indonesia You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed. A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms. Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars. The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. item.content:encoded: Generated Image. Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year. Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect. But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended. That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories. So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends: Bali, Indonesia You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed. A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms. Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars. The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. Some days, the entire plan may simply be breakfast, massage, swimming and sunset. And that is the itinerary . Private villa, poolside dinner, spa morning and sunset beach club–the perfect birthday idea. Thailand Thailand is for the celebrant who wants everything: City energy, beautiful beaches, nightlife, shopping, culture and food. It gives you enough value for money to stop your guests from sending angry voice notes about the budget. Begin in Bangkok. Give everyone time to arrive and recover. Host a rooftop welcome dinner overlooking the city. Then fly to Phuket or Krabi. Book a villa or resort close to the beach. Arrange a private yacht or traditional long-tail boat. Add island hopping and a birthday dinner by the sea. The birthday idea: Bangkok rooftop welcome, Phuket villa stay, private boat celebration and beach dinner. Mexico If you want a birthday everyone will still be talking about five years later, Mexico is for you. Cancún gives you all-inclusive resorts, beach clubs and nightlife. Tulum offers beautiful villas, restaurants and cenotes. Cabo brings dramatic coastline, polished resorts and excellent settings for sunset dinners and boat parties. For a milestone birthday, choose one base rather than trying to cover the entire country. Have a relaxed welcome evening. Settle in. Centre the birthday around a private catamaran followed by dinner on the beach. Then leave one day completely free. Trust me. A destination birthday should not feel like military service. The birthday idea: All-inclusive resort, catamaran celebration, beach dinner and one recovery day. Morocco There are birthday parties, then there are birthday scenes. Morocco gives you scenes. Picture everyone arriving at a beautiful riad in Marrakech. Lanterns glowing in the courtyard. Mint tea on arrival. Everyone admiring the architecture before immediately asking for the WiFi password. Spend a day exploring the souks or book a hammam experience. For the birthday itself, leave the city. Imagine a private desert dinner with music, candles and the Atlas Mountains in the background. Morocco already gives you colour, texture, food and atmosphere. You do not need to overproduce it. The birthday idea: Marrakech riad takeover, rooftop welcome dinner, hammam and private desert celebration. Jamaica Jamaica will always be personal for me. It is one of those places where celebration feels natural. Music is not added at the end. It is already part of the experience. It gives you a birthday that celebrates life, not just age. Rent a villa overlooking the Caribbean Sea. Arrange a jerk barbecue outside. Add a live reggae band or DJ. Spend one day on a catamaran and another exploring waterfalls. Then spend another doing absolutely nothing except eating, talking and enjoying the view. After forty or fifty years of life, perhaps that is exactly the point. The birthday idea: Private villa, Jamaican barbecue, live music, catamaran and waterfall excursion. Jordan Not every milestone birthday needs beach clubs and loud music; some deserve wonder. Imagine your group walking through the narrow Siq before Petra suddenly appears. Spend time floating in the Dead Sea. Book a night in Wadi Rum. Arrange a private desert dinner beneath the stars. Jordan works particularly well for smaller groups because the experience feels personal. Ten people is ideal, large enough to create energy and small enough to move comfortably. The birthday idea: Petra, Dead Sea relaxation and a private Wadi Rum desert dinner. Brazil Some destinations are beautiful; Brazil feels alive. Base yourself in Rio. Get an easy first evening of dinner, drinks and music. Then move between the beach, Sugarloaf Mountain, Christ the Redeemer, rooftop dinners and samba nights. For the birthday, arrange a private boat day followed by dinner with live Brazilian music. If you want deeper cultural connections, you can include Salvador for Afro-Brazilian heritage, food and music. Brazil will not reduce its energy simply because the celebrant is now forty or fifty. The birthday idea: Rio beach stay, private boat party, white dinner and live samba. Marbella, Spain If you have been paying attention to Nigerian destination celebrations recently, you may have noticed Marbella appearing more frequently. I understand why. In the last few months alone, Marbella has provided the backdrop for major Nigerian family celebrations and destination weddings. More recently, my team also worked with clients who chose Marbella for a 35th birthday celebration, bringing together a group of 20 people. For me, that was useful because Marbella moved from somewhere I could recommend in theory to somewhere I have now seen work for a Nigerian celebration group in practice. Marbella gives you many of the things Nigerians already love. Beautiful hotels and villas. Beach clubs, yachts, restaurants, nightlife, and sunshine. For a fortieth or fiftieth, I would give everyone an arrival day, have a proper welcome dinner, choose one or two major group experiences and leave enough space for people to enjoy Spain. Our recent group taught us something important: You do not need to programme every hour. Twenty adults will not necessarily want to wake up, eat, swim, shop and party at the same time. The bigger consideration for Nigerians planning Marbella in 2027 is the visa. Spain is within the Schengen Area, so Nigerian p

item.title: Steelers’ Jaquan Brisker hits Deshaun Watson with ‘babying’ jab after beating Browns
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Steelers’ Jaquan Brisker hits Deshaun Watson with ‘babying’ jab after beating Browns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns on Sunday , but Jaquan Brisker was not done going after Deshaun Watson even after the final whistle. On the third play of the game, the Steelers safety hit Watson high and was flagged for roughing the passer, handing Cleveland a fresh set of downs. The hit sent Watson to the medical tent for a concussion evaluation , and Shedeur Sanders stepped in for the rest of the series. Watson passed the evaluation and returned for the Browns’ next drive, but Brisker clearly did not think much of the call. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Babying the quarterback. He’s over there crying or whatever he’s doing. It is what it is,” Brisker said, via Ashley Wensk of KDKA-TV . Jaquan Brisker on getting flagged for roughing the passer for his hit on Deshaun Watson on the opening drive of Steelers/Browns "Babying the quarterback. He's over there crying or whatever he's doing. It is what it is." "He had his binky today, so." pic.twitter.com/6epqtF60Zd — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) November 1, 2026 Brisker then added another jab: “He had his binky today, so.” The flag aside, it was a long day for Watson and the Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh cruised to a 27-6 win, sacking Watson eight times and holding Cleveland out of the end zone for the first time this season. Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without a touchdown or an interception, but the Browns could not get anything going on the ground, finishing with just 34 rushing yards on 15 carries. Cleveland also lost two fumbles, while Pittsburgh’s defense racked up 13 quarterback hits and forced four three-and-outs. The Steelers, meanwhile, piled up 200 rushing yards. Rico Dowdle opened the scoring with a 9-yard touchdown run, Pat Freiermuth punched in a 1-yard score just before halftime and Jaylen Warren added another 1-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to make it 27-6. The win was a measure of revenge for Pittsburgh, which fell 27-24 to the Browns on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 . The Steelers improved to 6-2 and have now won four straight games, while the Browns dropped to 5-3. Brisker has quickly made his presence felt in Pittsburgh. The former second-round pick spent his first four seasons with the Chicago Bears before signing a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Steelers in March . His comments will likely add even more fuel to an already heated AFC North rivalry. The Steelers will have a week off before visiting the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football on Nov. 15. Related: Steelers’ Jaylen Warren throws shade at Jared Verse after dog-walking Browns Related: Steelers’ Cam Heyward scoffs at Jared Verse drama after smacking Browns

item.title: Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers have a name for their version of the tush push . They call it the “Nittany Package,” a nod to tight end Pat Freiermuth’s Penn State background. Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 on Sunday. With five seconds left, the Steelers had the ball at the 1-yard line. Aaron Rodgers chose to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal. Freiermuth took the direct snap and followed center Zach Frazier into the end zone. Tight end Darnell Washington and running back Jaylen Warren pushed him from behind. It gave Pittsburgh a 20-6 lead and was Freiermuth’s first rushing touchdown in six NFL seasons. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCarthy said Rodgers made the call . “Aaron called that play,” McCarthy said. “Obviously, everybody agreed with it. But the whole mechanics leading up to that, I think that just shows the confidence they have and, obviously, Aaron’s experience of handling those situations.” The Steelers have used the Nittany Package four times and converted on every attempt. They previously ran it on fourth-and-1 against the Patriots and Colts, and on third-and-1 against the Bengals. Sunday was their first attempt from the goal line. According to Rodgers, he was not leaving the field without trying to score. Pittsburgh had no timeouts left, so a failed attempt would have ended the half. Troy Fautanu also called it his favorite play. Pittsburgh had earlier failed to score from the Browns’ 2-yard line and settled for a field goal. McCarthy said he wished he could have those three plays back. But the Nittany Package worked when the Steelers tried it again on Sunday. Related: Steelers’ Jaylen Warren throws shade at Jared Verse after dog-walking Browns Related: Steelers’ Cam Heyward scoffs at Jared Verse drama after smacking Browns

item.title: Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) gets ready under center as the New York Jets play Las Vegas Raiders in a week 8 NFL football game at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in East Rutherford, NJ. Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kirk Cousins led the Las Vegas Raiders to a 38-33 road win over the New York Jets that came after a 23-14 halftime deficit that was sparked by a big day through the air from Brock Bowers . Coach Klint Kubiak commented on Ashton Jeanty ’s surprisingly low workload while Kirk Cousins was in a happy mood as he discussed his recently unveiled “wellness celly.” The Cousins celebration was on display with the Raiders trailing 30-21. Cousins mimicked an elbow massage as the Raiders attempted to claw their way back into the game. He talked to Megan Olivi about the move as fans watched. “We played through (adversity)…This league’s gonna test ya…I call that my wellness celebration, I told (teammates) if I had a rushing touchdown I’d do it, and Brock Bowers as I was jogging off the field, I wouldn’t have thought to do it, he goes, ‘Hit ’em with a wellness celly!’ So I did it.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cousins had over 200 yards and three touchdown passes as he focused on throwing to Bowers, Jeanty and Michael Mayer, working the field in sublime fashion as he led the Raiders back with possible replacement and 2026 NFL Draft first round pick Fernando Mendoza looking on. Jeanty took serious heat from Rex Ryan before the game about his comments on the Jets’ tackling abilities. He gave way to Mike Washington Jr. in the run game and he responded with 25 carries for 83 yards. Bowers had 92 yards and two touchdowns as the Raiders moved to 4-4. November 8 brings a home game against the San Francisco 49ers that will give Cousins a chance to take the starting QB job by the horns and restore confidence in fans moving forward. Related: Raiders news: Only 1 thing surprises Klint Kubiak about Brock Bowers after another big day Related: What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse

item.title: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams kept the Los Angeles Chargers winless, running away with a convincing win, 24-9, at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. The Rams improved to 4-4 , while the Chargers fell to 0-7. The Rams bucked a slow start, with Matthew Stafford throwing 17-of-25 for 157 yards and one touchdown, and Puka Nacua getting 11 receptions for 80 yards and a touchdown. After the encouraging performance, Nacua stressed that the Rams can still turn it up a notch, especially on offense, and go on a hot streak, according to the Los Angeles Daily News’ Adam Grosbard. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “This is something that we gotta be able to continue to build upon, but it’s not something that we can exhale from. There’s still a lot of improvement. If our defense is playing their butts off like that, we gotta be able to go out there and play complementary football,” said the 25-year-old wide receiver. The Rams lead the league with 411 yards per game. They average 24.3 points per outing, which is 10th in the NFL. The offense looked lethargic at the outset against the Chargers , failing to get a first down on their first five drives for the first time under coach Sean McVay. They went into the halftime break with a one-point lead, 10-9. The defense held down the fort, shutting down the Chargers in the second half. Justin Herbert finished 24-of-32 for zero touchdowns and two interceptions. He was sacked twice. The Rams won back-to-back games for the first time since January, beating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21, in Week 7. They will try to maintain their winning streak when they visit the Washington Commanders in Week 9. item.title: George Furbank: ‘A few people have said I need to go and see a witch doctor’
item.description: “A few people have said that I need to go and see a witch doctor,” George Furbank chuckles, perhaps to hide a grimace beneath after two years of misfortune. Rugby has known a few tales of black cats and broken mirrors but not many players have endured such a wretched run that has meant an absence from 20 consecutive England Tests in the prime of the full-back’s career. First came a broken arm in December of 2024; then a concussion; then a niggly calf injury he struggled to shake. In July, Furbank was named in the No 15 shirt for England’s encounter with South Africa only to be rushed to hospital to have his appendix removed – matchday was spent not at Ellis Park but in a rather different kind of Johannesburg theatre. “Do I believe in luck?” Furbank ponders, repeating the question I have posed with a contemplative pause. One would forgive an answer of frustration at this apparent cosmic misalignment but the 30-year-old is not that way minded. “Not really,” he continues. “It’s pretty cliche but I think you make your own luck. George Furbank has endured a tough two years (Getty) “Could you say I’ve been unlucky with the injuries and the timing? Potentially, but most boys will go through periods of injuries. Unfortunately, mine have been a bit back-to-back. The last two years have definitely been tough. I haven’t been able to play, or in good enough form to play, as much as I’d like to. But it has made me realise how much I do love coming here. I’m so desperate to be back on the international stage and pull on an England shirt again. When it gets taken away from you, you realise how much you miss it.” How England have missed Furbank, too. Their form may have fluctuated in the nearly two years since he won the last of his 14 caps against Japan but there has been a sense throughout that they might be a better side with the full-back in it. It is a mark of Steve Borthwick ’s faith in the player that he has remained a contracted player throughout his injury trials and tribulations; all will hope for a clean bill of health throughout this November. Furbank has suffered a number of different injuries (PA Wire) It has been a year of change in other ways for Furbank. If it was a wrench to leave Northampton with club and captain unable to reach agreement on mutually beneficial terms, another Gallagher Prem title was a perfect farewell , and Furbank has settled well at Harlequins. A house in Wimbledon has fulfilled a life-long dream to live in London – if Northampton had its small-town charm, the comparative cornucopia on his new doorstep is providing a welcome alternative. “Finishing the way I did at Saints was special, and a pretty cool way to close that chapter in my life.
