item.content:encoded: “A few people have said that I need to go and see a witch doctor,” George Furbank chuckles, perhaps to hide a grimace beneath after two years of misfortune. Rugby has known a few tales of black cats and broken mirrors but not many players have endured such a wretched run that has meant an absence from 20 consecutive England Tests in the prime of the full-back’s career. First came a broken arm in December of 2024; then a concussion; then a niggly calf injury he struggled to shake. In July, Furbank was named in the No 15 shirt for England’s encounter with South Africa only to be rushed to hospital to have his appendix removed – matchday was spent not at Ellis Park but in a rather different kind of Johannesburg theatre. “Do I believe in luck?” Furbank ponders, repeating the question I have posed with a contemplative pause. One would forgive an answer of frustration at this apparent cosmic misalignment but the 30-year-old is not that way minded. “Not really,” he continues. “It’s pretty cliche but I think you make your own luck. George Furbank has endured a tough two years (Getty) “Could you say I’ve been unlucky with the injuries and the timing? Potentially, but most boys will go through periods of injuries. Unfortunately, mine have been a bit back-to-back. The last two years have definitely been tough. I haven’t been able to play, or in good enough form to play, as much as I’d like to. But it has made me realise how much I do love coming here. I’m so desperate to be back on the international stage and pull on an England shirt again. When it gets taken away from you, you realise how much you miss it.” How England have missed Furbank, too. Their form may have fluctuated in the nearly two years since he won the last of his 14 caps against Japan but there has been a sense throughout that they might be a better side with the full-back in it. It is a mark of Steve Borthwick ’s faith in the player that he has remained a contracted player throughout his injury trials and tribulations; all will hope for a clean bill of health throughout this November. Furbank has suffered a number of different injuries (PA Wire) It has been a year of change in other ways for Furbank. If it was a wrench to leave Northampton with club and captain unable to reach agreement on mutually beneficial terms, another Gallagher Prem title was a perfect farewell , and Furbank has settled well at Harlequins. A house in Wimbledon has fulfilled a life-long dream to live in London – if Northampton had its small-town charm, the comparative cornucopia on his new doorstep is providing a welcome alternative. “Finishing the way I did at Saints was special, and a pretty cool way to close that chapter in my life. But this has rejuvenated me,” Furbank explains. “A new challenge, new coaches, new players, a bit of a different way of playing. That group at Saints was so tight. We did stuff with each other every single day off. “I was a little bit worried – the boys are spread across so many different areas of London. Is it going to be that same feeling? It is a little bit different because boys are everywhere. But there’s still a really good environment. There’s always someone wanting to go for coffee.” The Hand-in-Hand pub on the common and Demitasse on the high street are becoming regular haunts. Furbank signed off with a second Prem title at Northampton (Getty) Alas, certain things did travel south with Furbank. His first outing in the quarters was over almost before it began after being knocked out by a stray knee against Edinburgh – “A good start to my Quins career! 30 seconds into my first game…” – and a delayed debut in the Prem for his new employers ended with a 48-0 thrashing by Gloucester. But things are starting to turn: Furbank was an influential presence in wins over Saracens and Exeter , and Harlequins have made a strong start in the Challenge Cup, a competition of real focus this season. The 30-year-old sees a resemblance to the struggles Saints experienced before the transformative impact of Chris Boyd, Phil Dowson and Sam Vesty, and hopes for a similarly effective turnaround. He is enjoying, too, the chance to combine more closely with Marcus Smith, a kindred spirit. “He’s world class to work with. He does things on the pitch that not many people can do. His dedication off the pitch in constantly improving his game is special as well.” Furbank has settled well at Harlequins (Getty) Could their alliance be reprised internationally? Regardless of the exact personnel, England’s playmaking partnership will surely be key to their Nations Championship fortunes. Borthwick’s squad are under no illusions that these Tests will be tighter and tougher than the games experienced in a fast and loose start to the Prem campaign, but a capacity to create and exploit space will clearly be vital. Furbank, though, wants no part of the criticism that has accompanied a high-scoring first phase of the season. “It kind of does my head in a bit. You have a season where there is a lot of kicking and defences are dominant, everyone moans about that. Then you have a 71-48 game, people are moaning about that. Find something to enjoy! “I watched that Saints-Bath game and could appreciate some unbelievable attack on show. But then you watch Gloucester-Bath, which is again incredible to watch but completely different. Why can’t you appreciate both? Teams are going to play differently depending on how they think they can get the best out of their players. Furbank last featured for England in November 2024 (Getty) “You watch the NRL and it always seems focused on, ‘how good was that?’ I think if you look at everything negatively the whole time, you don’t get any enjoyment or excitement out of the game. Yes, there are bits you have got to critique, don’t get me wrong, but I also think we can be way more positive in how we play and watch the game.” It is with that positive mindset that Furbank intends to attack the year ahead. Having made his debut in the Six Nations after the 2019 World Cup but fallen out of favour by the time of the next tournament, a trip to Australia next year is in the back of his mind. He can just about recall England’s last World Cup Down Under – the 2002/03 triumph. Furbank hopes to be part of England's squad at next year's World Cup (Getty) “I’d have been seven. I remember bits. I was down at Huntingdon Rugby Club watching it in a full clubhouse. I remember being quite overwhelmed when that drop goal went over; I think beer went flying everywhere, which probably wasn’t what a seven-year-old needed… “I don’t actively think about it but it is something in the background that is on my mind. It’s one of the goals I’ve got left in rugby: to go to a World Cup with England, and win a World Cup with England. That is the pinnacle of anyone’s career. It’s something that would be an absolute dream. To be that team to go and win it again would be incredibly special.”

item.title: 10 Eagles things I think I think from the loss to the Commanders
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts to a unnecessary roughness penalty by K'lavon Chaisson #45 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles certainly put up a performance for the ages on Sunday Night Football. This was a game where the Eagles needed a win to salvage a season that was on the verge of cratering, and they certainly imploded. Philadelphia’s offense barely mustered 10 points against the Washington Commanders in a 27-10 loss, while the defense allowed 27 unanswered points after the Eagles took a 10-0 lead late in the first quarter. The Eagles weren’t even competitive against a Commanders team that had just 1 win heading into November. That’s how bad this Eagles team is. While the season isn’t at the halfway point yet, this Eagles season is essentially over. There’s little confidence this team is going to make a run in the lowly NFC East, not with how poor they have played during this six-game losing streak (which is the longest by this franchise since 2012). The Eagles have started 2-6 for the first time since 1999, and there are a lot of aspects from this horrendous performance that need to be dissected. Buckle up. There are some hard truths coming regarding this football team. 1) This offensive line has gotten significantly worse under Chris Kuper. Jeff Stoutland might be the best assistant coach in franchise history. The Eagles were never going to replace him. Unfortunately, the Eagles found an offensive line coach that doesn’t improve his players — at all. Under Kuper, two of the five starting offensive linemen (Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen) from last season have gotten worse and the two young players (Markel Bell and Drew Kendall) are struggling to improve week in and week out. Bell was abysmal against the Commanders, allowing a 7.0% pressure rate and two sacks while getting dominated by K’Lavon Chaisson all night. Replacing Lane Johnson in a rookie season is a tough task, but Bell is not ready to be a starting right tackle in the NFL. That’s on Kuper and how he’s developing a rookie who is learning how to play right tackle for the first time in his football life. Dickerson allowed a sack and a 4.7% pressure rate, and his pressure rate is 7.8% in the three games he played this seaosn. This was a Pro Bowl player under Stoutland and now he’s a replacement level guard. Jordan Mailata’s performance is even diminishing, as he allowed a 7.0% pressure rate against the Commanders in what wa shis worst game of the season. If the Eagles do decide to move on from a coach this month, Kuper should be the first candidate. 2) The Eagles were right about Tanner McKee this summer. McKee lost out to Andy Dalton in the battle for the QB2 job for a reason. There is enough tape in the three games to demonstrate McKee isn’t good enough to be a starting quarterback
item.content:encoded: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts to a unnecessary roughness penalty by K'lavon Chaisson #45 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles certainly put up a performance for the ages on Sunday Night Football. This was a game where the Eagles needed a win to salvage a season that was on the verge of cratering, and they certainly imploded. Philadelphia’s offense barely mustered 10 points against the Washington Commanders in a 27-10 loss, while the defense allowed 27 unanswered points after the Eagles took a 10-0 lead late in the first quarter. The Eagles weren’t even competitive against a Commanders team that had just 1 win heading into November. That’s how bad this Eagles team is. While the season isn’t at the halfway point yet, this Eagles season is essentially over. There’s little confidence this team is going to make a run in the lowly NFC East, not with how poor they have played during this six-game losing streak (which is the longest by this franchise since 2012). The Eagles have started 2-6 for the first time since 1999, and there are a lot of aspects from this horrendous performance that need to be dissected. Buckle up. There are some hard truths coming regarding this football team. 1) This offensive line has gotten significantly worse under Chris Kuper. Jeff Stoutland might be the best assistant coach in franchise history. The Eagles were never going to replace him. Unfortunately, the Eagles found an offensive line coach that doesn’t improve his players — at all. Under Kuper, two of the five starting offensive linemen (Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen) from last season have gotten worse and the two young players (Markel Bell and Drew Kendall) are struggling to improve week in and week out. Bell was abysmal against the Commanders, allowing a 7.0% pressure rate and two sacks while getting dominated by K’Lavon Chaisson all night. Replacing Lane Johnson in a rookie season is a tough task, but Bell is not ready to be a starting right tackle in the NFL. That’s on Kuper and how he’s developing a rookie who is learning how to play right tackle for the first time in his football life. Dickerson allowed a sack and a 4.7% pressure rate, and his pressure rate is 7.8% in the three games he played this seaosn. This was a Pro Bowl player under Stoutland and now he’s a replacement level guard. Jordan Mailata’s performance is even diminishing, as he allowed a 7.0% pressure rate against the Commanders in what wa shis worst game of the season. If the Eagles do decide to move on from a coach this month, Kuper should be the first candidate. 2) The Eagles were right about Tanner McKee this summer. McKee lost out to Andy Dalton in the battle for the QB2 job for a reason. There is enough tape in the three games to demonstrate McKee isn’t good enough to be a starting quarterback in the league. Even with the offensive line decimated by injuries and a poor offensive line, McKee is slow in his progressions and has no mobility to get out of trouble. McKee was abysmal against the Commanders, finishing 23-of-34 for 212 yards with 0 TD, 1 INT and a 72.2 passer rating. He also had a lost fumble in the second half, giving McKee two giveaways on the night. The numbers should have been worse, but 46 passing yards where in garbage time in the final minute to Eli Stowers. Since McKee made his first start in Week 6, he’s completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with 2 TD, 2 INT, and a 76.6 passer rating. McKee is 31st out of 32 quarterbacks in yards per attempt (5.6) and 26th in passer rating. The Eagles offense are 32nd in yards per play (4.2) in the three games with McKee as the starting quarterback, 31st in yards per attempt (5.6), and 29th in offensive points per game (15.0). McKee isn’t the answer as a starting quarterback. He may not even be a QB2 at this rate. The Eagles could try Joe Milton, but the offense won’t move the ball with him either. 3) The second half offense still stinks. Another week the Eagles offense struggled in the second half. Before the Eagles hit the garbage time portion of the game (27-10), the offense ran 32 plays for 91 yards with two giveaways, a missed field goal, and zero points — an abysmal 2.8 yards per play. Whether Jalen Hurts or Tanner McKee is the quarterback, this offense doesn’t move the ball. The Eagles average just 4.6 points per game in the second half, which is last in the nFL. The Eagles are also last in yards per play (3.9), yards per game (116.3), and yards per attempt (5.5). They are 29th in yards per carry (3.4), 30th in passer rating (70.4), and 29th in sack rate allowed (10.4%). McKee was 10-of-14 for 58 yards with 0 TD, 1 INT and a 49.1 passer rating in the second half prior to the garbage time possession at the end of the game — 4.1 yards per attempt. He led the Eagles with 16 rushing yards in the second half at that point, as Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell had 11 carries for 29 yards. Simply put, the Eagles aren’t making adjustments. 4) The second half defense is slightly better. This unit is bad too. They just aren’t at the very bottom of the league like the offense is. The Eagles are 30th in the NFL in points per game allowed (14.1) and 31st in yards per game allowed (198.1). They are 29th in yards per play allowed (5.9) and 32nd in rush yards per game allowed (78.1). The pass rush in the second half isn’t good either, as they are 27th in pressure rate (29.9%) and 27th in sack rate (4.6%). The pass defense is 29th in yards per attempt allowed (8.0). Again, they aren’t at the very bottom of the league. The second half defense is just near the bottom. This is a huge reason why the 2026 Eagles lose football games. 5) In conclusion… The Eagles are arguably the worst second half team in all of football, being outscored 113 to 37 in the second half of games this season. That -76 point differential isn’t even the worst in the NFL, as the Baltimore Ravens sit at -87 following their blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills this week (and the Ravens are on their third-string quarterback too). The yardage differential in the second half of games is -655, worst in the league. The next closest team are the Ravens at -629. The time of possession margin is -2.55 (29th), while the points per drive is 0.84 (32nd), and the three-and-out percentage is 50.0% (32nd). The explosive plays aren’t even there, as the 2.9% 20+ yard play percentage is 32nd in the league. Somehow the Eagles get worse in the second half of games. The personnel isn’t there (at least on one side of the ball), but the struggles go much deeper than that. 6) The run defense is making history. Another week the Eagles defense has allowed 100+ rushing yards to an opponent, as the Commanders had 135 rushing yards against a run defense that was supposed to be a strength of this team entering the year. Instead, the run defense is historically bad — and on the wrong side of history. The Eagles have allowed 100+ rushing yards in each of the first eight games of a season for the first time since 1968, and only the second time in the Super Bowl era. That 1968 team was one of the worst in franchise history, as the Eagles started 0-11 and finished 2-12. They weren’t even bad enough to get the No. 1 pick that year, and the fanbase booed Santa Claus that December as a result. The Eagles have allowed 1,055 rushing yards through eight games, third most in the NFL. The 131.9 rushing yards per game is also 30th, and the most by an Eagles team through eight games since 1998 (146.3). That 1998 Eagles team finished 3-13. This Eagles team is staring at a record that bad based on how poor the run defense is. 7) It’s time to protect Saquon Barkley from himself. Barkley deserves plenty of credit for fighting through his hamstring and back injuries and gutting out performances f

Milan are working hard to get him to sign and want to tie him down ," said Fabrizio Romano on the future of the French midfielder, whose renewal is set to become a priority for the Rossoneri's management. Meanwhile, attention is already turning to the January transfer window. After failing to sign a defender in the summer, the club could make another move for Gonçalo Inácio , a player previously linked with the Rossoneri who remains highly rated. The issue remains finding a fifth striker, a topic back in the spotlight following the attacking crisis caused by injuries to Lautaro Martinez , Bonny and Pio Esposito. Inter had already assessed several options in the summer but chose not to proceed because they were unconvinced by the players available. The idea was to add a forward with different qualities from the four already in the squad, rather than a traditional centre-forward. Now the situation has changed, and the club and coach will have to assess whether to enter the transfer market. 😨 Napoli worried about KDB! Tests today There is concern at Napoli over Kevin De Bruyne , who was forced off at half-time against Juventus. The Belgian midfielder suffered a sprained ankle and, despite asking for painkillers to try to continue, the pain forced him to stop. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , he will undergo scans today to determine the extent of the injury and establish a recovery timeline. His availability for Wednesday's match in Portugal against Porto is in serious doubt. It would be a major absence for Napoli, who risk losing another quality player at a particularly delicate stage of the season, with several fixtures in quick succession before the international break. 🤔 Roma: who will play in Manchester? Roma have arrived in England to prepare for their clash with Manchester United at Old Trafford. Following the press conference with Gasperini and De Roon , the Giallorossi will hold their final training session at the Red Devils' stadium this evening. Some changes are expected from the win over Udinese, although the absences of Svilar, Dybala, Koné and Pellegrini remain a major blow. The goalkeeper will not return until after the international break, while the number seven is expected to be sidelined until January. Dybala and Koné, meanwhile, hope to recover for Saturday's match against Sassuolo. Gollini will remain in goal, while Mancini is ready to return in defence alongside Ndicka and Hermoso. De Roon and Cristante will continue their midfield partnership, with Malen and Soulé guaranteed places in attack. The main doubts concern the flanks, where Wesley is certain to start, but which side he plays on remains to be decided: Lulli, Rensch and Molina are in contention. Finally, in attacking midfield, Pisilli appears to be ahead of Mora, despite the young former Porto player having scored in two consecutive games. 🤕 Lazio: an update on Cataldi Lazio also saw off Cagliari, claiming three crucial points that put them alone at the top following Inter's defeat. The Biancocelesti initially fell behind at the Olimpico but turned the game around thanks to goals from Isaksen and Pinamonti , maintaining the fine form of Gattuso 's side. The evening also marked the return of Danilo Cataldi , who finally made his first appearance of the season. The midfielder settled into the game well but was seen limping at the final whistle. According to Lazio Style Channel , the number 32 suffered heavy bruising: it does not appear to be a cause for concern, but further checks will be needed in the coming hours to assess his condition. 😕 Fiorentina: Fagioli and Oulai together? Nicolò Fagioli remains a mainstay for Fiorentina, with 734 minutes played and 10 starts in the first 11 matches of the season. Among outfield players, only Mastantuono, Ndour and Dragusin have played more minutes. However, criticism following the Atalanta match, combined with Oulai 's impressive performance off the bench, has reignited the debate over whether they can play together. In the first two and a half months, the pair shared the pitch for just 80 minutes across three defeats: Genoa was the only game they started together. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , Vanoli is looking for a way to accommodate both, but the team's midfield struggles have so far limited his experiments. One possibility is to give Oulai the deep-lying playmaker role, moving Fagioli into a wider central midfield position, with Ndour or Brescianini on the other side. Trials could be postponed until after the international break, while the club are already considering further midfield reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window. item.title: Hansi Flick set to repeat Barcelona defensive experiment against Aston Villa – report
item.description: Hansi Flick set to repeat Barcelona defensive experiment against Aston Villa – report Barcelona manager Hansi Flick could once again turn to Frenkie de Jong and Brian Farinas in unfamiliar defensive roles when the Catalans host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday, November 3. According to a report from AS , the German coach is considering retaining the makeshift defensive combination after it helped Barcelona secure a 6-1 victory over Alaves at Camp Nou . Flick’s decision against Alaves was dictated by an injury crisis that has left Barcelona short of defensive options. On that note, the likes of Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen were unavailable, while Xavi Espart was also among the absentees. With limited alternatives, the manager deployed De Jong at left centre-back and handed Farinas his first-team debut at right-back, despite the youngster being a midfielder by trade. Barcelona defensive injuries leave Flick with limited options The situation has forced Flick to experiment with the available options as he attempts to maintain defensive stability during an important period of the season. Frenkie de Jong played as a centre-back against Alaves. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) De Jong’s technical quality makes him a useful option when Barcelona need to build attacks from the back, although playing regularly as a centre-back would be a significant change to his responsibilities. Farinas, meanwhile, has an opportunity to demonstrate his versatility after being trusted with an unexpected first-team assignment. Barcelona’s 6-1 victory over Alaves offered encouragement, but the result does not necessarily mean the experimental defensive partnership has resolved the team’s underlying problems. In fact, the expectation is that the challenge against Aston Villa will provide a different level of examination. Farinas faces competition despite impressive debut Farinas’ involvement is particularly interesting because competition for midfield places at Barcelona is already intense. On that note, De Jong, Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal and Rodri are among the options ahead of him, while Espart can also operate in midfield. Brian Farinas made his Barcelona debut as a right-back. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Consequently, the youngster’s route into the senior side could be strengthened through his ability to cover multiple positions. item.title: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho
item.description: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho Real Madrid have seen a massive turnaround in their fortunes in the last few weeks, making it six wins in a row with victory over Racing Santander. Los Blancos came flying out of the blocks at El Sardinero and scored three goals in the first half, which was enough for them to secure the three points. Among the many players who had a great game was Arda Guler, who continued his impressive start to the season. While Kylian Mbappe continues to dominate the goalscoring headlines, the Turkish international is quietly establishing himself as the creative spark of the team. Guler leads La Liga in two creative statistics Guler has registered 39 key passes and 21 accurate crosses this season, leading La Liga in both metrics. His numbers underline just how important and undroppable he has become for Jose Mourinho, making that right-wing position his own. The 21-year-old has also accumulated 4.32 expected assists (xA), the second-highest tally in the competition. His tally of 12 big chances created also places him second among La Liga players this season. Despite these numbers, the Turkish international has only three assists to his name, including one in the 3-0 victory over Racing. Against Racing, Guler provided a perfectly weighted through ball for Jude Bellingham’s well-taken goal. Three assists don’t paint the whole picture Guler’s underlying numbers suggest his influence and assist tally should have been much greater than just three. Expected assists is a measure of the quality of chances he has created, and the fact that his actual assists fall short of that figure suggests his teammates have not been clinical enough. Most leading assist providers in football tend to register more assists than their xA suggests, but Guler is an exception. Arda Guler has been Real Madrid’s creative force this season. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) However, if the finishing falls into place, it is encouraging that Guler’s underlying numbers are so promising. Mourinho trusts him a lot, and his ability to drift inside, identify passing lanes and deliver inch-perfect crosses provides the perfect balance for Madrid’s transitional attackers. Guler is also an exceptional set-piece taker, always posing a threat from both free kicks and corners. The 21-year-old is slowly evolving from a talented youngster into one of the first names on Mourinho’s team sheet , and it remains to be seen how he fares over the course of the season.

item.title: No Grealish, no cry - the rise of Everton's youngsters
item.description: Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season [Getty Images] As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high. A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes. Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training. The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years. Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney. A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley. Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career. After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves. The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season. David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground. "I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be]. "But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball. "But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair." While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season. Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry. item.content:encoded: Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season [Getty Images] As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high. A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes. Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training. The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years. Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney. A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley. Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career. After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves. The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season. David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground. "I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be]. "But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball. "But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair." While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season. Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry. The France Under-21 international is playing just a third season in a top-five European league after joining from Villarreal in July 2025, but his introduction to elite football has been more pressurised because of Everton's lack of options up front. Barry is the club's only specialist centre-forward, starting every match and playing 918 minutes this season. His tally of seven goals is already just one off his total from last season, despite playing 30 fewer matches. Everton have recorded 24 big chances, and Barry has been involved in 15 of them (62.5%). Whiles Moyes' hand has been somewhat forced in giving Barry game time because of a lack of alternatives, there has been a broader indication he is more prepared to back the younger members of his squad this season. The average age of Everton's starting XI in the Premier League has dropped by almost 18 months this season to 26 years and 216 days. The departure of veteran midfielder Idrissa Gueye has made a difference but first-team players aged 24 or under are playing a much higher proportion of Premier League minutes than in the previous campaign. Moyes used just 22 players in the Premier League last season. He has already used 22 in this one. Even the youngest players in the squad appear to have gained more trust. In 2025-26, players aged 21 or under totalled 1,088 minutes for the Toffees, a figure that has already been exceeded this season (1,206). At 19, Harrison Armstrong is the youngest regular in Everton's senior squad. In January, he had completed a six-month loan spell at Preston and Moyes considered sending him back to Deepdale for the remainder of last season before slowly integrating him into the first team. This season, the teenager has started every Premier League match. Winger Tyler Dibling, 20, initially struggled after a £35m move from Southampton in the summer of 2025 but was positive in getting Everton on to the front foot on against Newcastle on Thursday night. Tyrique George joined on a permanent deal from Chelsea in the summer after spending the second half of last season on loan at Everton during which he made only one league start. The 20-year-old has already made five this season, scoring his first goal for the club in the 2-2 draw with Manchester United in September. George also started the EFL Cup fixture last week and won back possession for the opening goal. Merlin Rohl broke into the team towards the end of last season and the 24-year-old midfielder, who also signed permanently in the summer following an initial loan spell, has since been trusted to fill Everton's problem position of right-back. After missing four games because of injury, he was immediately brought back into the starting XI against Chelsea. He was then preferred to the more experienced Ainsley Maitland-Niles at right-back for matches against Arsenal and Newcastle. When asked if Grealish would return to the squad for Monday's rematch at St James' Park, Moyes said he would not reveal any team news, though there is no doubt that experience still counts among the 63-year-old's most valuable commodities. Defender James Tarkowksi, 33, has been a standout performer so far this season, while the form of fellow senior players such as Jordan Pickford, 32, and Dewsbury-Hall, 28 remain critical to this Everton side. But when Everton meet Newcastle for the second time in less than a week on Monday, Grealish could again miss out. In his absence, younger heads were good enough to win a cup tie. It would be further indication of their growing influence if they were to repeat that result in the Premier League. Everton striker's relief family not home during burglary Britain's first £100m man facing defining moment

item.title: Evan Turner has just one thing to say about Giannis Antetokounmpo after watching Cooper Flagg
item.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images Evan Turner has made a bold statement about Giannis Antetokounmpo after Cooper Flagg’s brilliant start to his second season. The Dallas Mavericks teenager was brilliant in the last campaign and deservedly won the Rookie of the Year award. This season, he has taken his game to the next level. That has led to a lot of praise from many big names in the game, but the boldest one may have just come from Turner. Evan Turner says Cooper Flagg is better than Giannis Antetokounmpo Flagg’s Mavericks and Antetokounmpo’s Heat faced each other recently, and the two players put on a show. Both of them scored 29 points and recorded 11 assists for their respective sides, but Dallas edged the game by four points in the end. Antetokounmpo is regarded by many as one of the best in the game, but Turner believes Flagg looked even better than him, despite being nearly half his age. Speaking on the Open Floor NBA Talk show , the former 76ers guard said: “Hey, I was sceptical, bro, but Cooper… He could have had 40-something. He literally was getting his guys in like that. Hey, that’s a bad boy, bro. “When I saw it, I said, man, he is better than Giannis. And Giannis is in old-school attack mode. And Cooper was on some chill ‘I know how to win’ type. Like, did you feel that? He was almost like: ‘Wait, I know how to win.’ “He literally turned it on, and he was going at Wiggins, then taking it into the paint on Giannis. Like, he was being nice that night. He should have had a 40-point triple. That boy is cold. He’s here.” Turner concluded by saying: “It looked like, correct me if I’m wrong, it looked like he was hooping with his little bros. Like, it looked like he was hooping on a smaller rim.” Flagg really is a superstar in the making, but he still has a lot to learn and achieve before he can be spoken about in the same breath as Antetokounmpo. However, early signs really are positive, and Dallas Mavericks fans have every reason to be excited about their young prodigy. item.title: Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers
item.description: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams cruised past the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday , but Sean McVay could not resist poking a little fun at Aaron Donald for one play that got away from the future Hall of Famer. Late in the third quarter of the Rams’ 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium, undrafted rookie linebacker Wesley Bailey strip-sacked Justin Herbert at the Chargers’ 26-yard line. The loose ball bounced right toward Donald, giving him a chance at a scoop-and-score. Instead, the 35-year-old tried to scoop it up near the 20 and whiffed. He stumbled, fell on the ball and knocked it out of bounds, allowing the Chargers to keep possession after a 9-yard loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McVay was all smiles when asked about the play after the game. “Oh man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that,” McVay said, via Adam Grosbard of the Los Angeles Daily News. “He couldn’t even look at me. At least we can laugh about it right now.” The Rams head coach also told radio play-by-play voice J.B. Long that he was going to “crush him” for the missed opportunity. It would have been a special moment for Donald, who has never scored a touchdown in his NFL career. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year retired in March 2024 after 10 seasons, only to come back this summer on a one-year, $20 million deal . His return made the Rams’ defensive front even scarier alongside Myles Garrett , whom Los Angeles acquired from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason. Donald has still made his share of plays this season. In the Rams’ Week 5 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, he fell on a fumble forced by Nate Landman to give Los Angeles the ball with a chance to win. The miss did not cost the Rams on Sunday. Los Angeles held the Chargers scoreless after halftime, intercepted Herbert twice and dropped the Chargers to 0-7 for the first time since Jim Harbaugh was their quarterback . The Rams improved to 4-4 with their second straight win. Donald will look for another chance at his first career touchdown when the Rams visit the Washington Commanders next Sunday. Related: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns Related: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers

item.title: ‘Coming Together And Working Hard’ – How Christian Lee Is Paving The Way For Hawaii’s Next Generation Of Fighters
item.description: Christian “The Warrior” Lee has reached the absolute pinnacle of mixed martial arts. Now, the two-division ONE World Champion is actively laying the foundation for a new generation of Hawaiian athletes to do the same. The 28-year-old began his martial arts journey as a teenage debutant and today reigns supreme over both the lightweight and welterweight MMA divisions. Away from the global spotlight, a deeply personal chapter continues to grow: he and his wife, Katie, recently welcomed their fourth child into the world. View this post on Instagram Before his story continues, a massive assignment in Bangkok’s iconic Lumpinee Stadium awaits. Lee will defend his lightweight MMA gold against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo in the main event of The Inner Circle 37 on Friday, November 6. The Asia primetime blockbuster will be exclusively available to subscribers at live.onefc.com . While the global fan base sees the heavy gold wrapped around his waist, fewer witness the grueling early mornings dedicated to helping eager local students dare to dream bigger. Building A Home For Local Talent Christian Lee co-owns Prodigy Training Center in Waipahu, Hawaii, alongside his wife. The family gym, which he formally rebranded in 2024, has rapidly evolved into a vital rallying point for martial artists across the island. Named in loving tribute to his late sister, the facility is built entirely around lifting others up. “The Warrior” coaches students of every skill level on those mats, partnering with his younger brother, Adrian “The Phenom” Lee , to bring the elite techniques they hone in global competition directly back to their community. Lee told onefc.com: “The gym’s doing great. We’ve had a lot of guys competing, and a lot of guys winning their fights, too. We’re just building up a strong community, those who just enjoy training and enjoy martial arts. “We’ve got a strong youth team, and we’re getting some kids ready to start their amateur youth MMA careers. So we have a few rising pros, and a few amateurs that are getting ready to turn pro as well.” View this post on Instagram Givi
item.content:encoded: Christian “The Warrior” Lee has reached the absolute pinnacle of mixed martial arts. Now, the two-division ONE World Champion is actively laying the foundation for a new generation of Hawaiian athletes to do the same. The 28-year-old began his martial arts journey as a teenage debutant and today reigns supreme over both the lightweight and welterweight MMA divisions. Away from the global spotlight, a deeply personal chapter continues to grow: he and his wife, Katie, recently welcomed their fourth child into the world. View this post on Instagram Before his story continues, a massive assignment in Bangkok’s iconic Lumpinee Stadium awaits. Lee will defend his lightweight MMA gold against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo in the main event of The Inner Circle 37 on Friday, November 6. The Asia primetime blockbuster will be exclusively available to subscribers at live.onefc.com . While the global fan base sees the heavy gold wrapped around his waist, fewer witness the grueling early mornings dedicated to helping eager local students dare to dream bigger. Building A Home For Local Talent Christian Lee co-owns Prodigy Training Center in Waipahu, Hawaii, alongside his wife. The family gym, which he formally rebranded in 2024, has rapidly evolved into a vital rallying point for martial artists across the island. Named in loving tribute to his late sister, the facility is built entirely around lifting others up. “The Warrior” coaches students of every skill level on those mats, partnering with his younger brother, Adrian “The Phenom” Lee , to bring the elite techniques they hone in global competition directly back to their community. Lee told onefc.com: “The gym’s doing great. We’ve had a lot of guys competing, and a lot of guys winning their fights, too. We’re just building up a strong community, those who just enjoy training and enjoy martial arts. “We’ve got a strong youth team, and we’re getting some kids ready to start their amateur youth MMA careers. We’re bringing them overseas to California next year. So, yeah, it’s been great.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship That grassroots guidance extends far beyond the amateur ranks. Lee is actively helping fellow athletes make the difficult leap to the professional circuit, and virtually no one is better positioned to show them the way. At just 20 years old, he became the youngest-ever male MMA World Champion when he dethroned Shinya “Tobikan Judan” Aoki for the lightweight gold in May 2019. Seven years later, he is paying that invaluable experience forward, guiding Hawaii’s next wave of fighters toward the exact dreams he once chased himself. He continued: “We had a few amateur fighters. One of my guys just fought in the California amateur show. He won. Another one of my guys just fought; he had a pro match in the States, and he won his third MMA match. So we have a few rising pros, and a few amateurs that are getting ready to turn pro as well.” View this post on Instagram Giving An Island Its Stage Christian Lee understands that geographic distance can often serve as a Hawaiian fighter’s toughest opponent. Oahu sits roughly 2,400 miles from San Francisco, one of the closest points on the U.S. mainland, requiring nearly six hours in the air to reach any major hub. For a young athlete, every chance to prove themselves is a very long, expensive trip away. With no active amateur MMA promotions left on the island, Lee decided to fill the glaring void himself, cultivating opportunities in the very place where his family’s renowned fighting legacy originally took root. The two-division MMA World Champion shared: “We just held an event in our gym, and we call it a smoker event. Basically, we hold fights in our gym – no winner, no loser – but we get to see who the better fighter is, and we encourage our guys to go for the finish. So we matchmade a whole card. “We had, like, 15 matches, MMA and kickboxing, and we had 10 of our guys from our gym competing in that, and most of them all won their matches, so it was a great event. We had like 400 people in the gym watching.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship The heavy cost of that geographic gap becomes obvious when the island’s raw talents are forced to leave. According to Lee, many aspiring pros head to places like Las Vegas in search of resources. The homegrown athletes who do fly out often face opponents holding vastly more experience, simply because mainland athletes can easily drive from state to state picking up fights every weekend. Lee’s in-house events are his direct method of leveling those odds. For a hungry up-and-comer, a packed night competing inside Prodigy Training Center is much more than practice. It is tangible proof that someone believes they belong in the sport. “The Warrior” added: “These guys train really hard, but there’s no promotion. So we do these types of events so that they can get the fighting experience they need, and then travel overseas from Hawaii, and then they’ll be ready. I’m happy that we’re able to play a part in that. “It’s some work, it definitely is, especially with this fight coming up. I definitely had a lot to think about, but it was a great event, the turnout was great, and I’m happy to do that because in Hawaii, there’s no platform for all of the guys on the island to fight.” View this post on Instagram A Culture Worth Fighting For Christian Lee has seen firsthand that the island’s deep-rooted hunger to compete never faded. Across Hawaii, athletes fiercely love to train in MMA, kickboxing, boxing, wrestling, and grappling. He sees a local scene desperate for a larger stage. The Prodigy Training Center head honcho grew up immersed in that exact culture, and he remembers precisely what steady competition meant to his own development as a teenager. Now, “The Warrior” is determined to provide the next generation of local hopefuls with a similar launching pad. Lee said: “When I was 15, I was able to fight three times a month. And now these guys who are wanting to fight, I see that there’s definitely a need for it. So I’m happy that we can put on events like this. And when we have like 30 guys competing, they’re all in the gym, and there’s not a single altercation in the gym. “It’s great to see everyone coming together from different gyms, and just being happy to have that platform to fight, to get where they want to go. A lot of these guys, really, their dream is to be pro fighters.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship No significant movement is ever carried by just one person, and Lee keeps elite company. His younger brother coaches directly alongside him, and his wife, Katie, ensures the business operations run seamlessly. Beyond the immediate gym walls, the island’s absolute best have joined the cause, including multi-time MMA World Champion Max Holloway. The 28-year-old reflected: “We’ve been blessed to have a lot of support from my friends over the years. Max has been coming in regularly to train and to help give me looks in the room. And another good friend, Ray Cooper, has been coming in, too. “Between the three of us – me, Max, and Ray – we’re like the seasoned fighters coming out of Hawaii who still live and train out of Hawaii. Despite all of the odds against us out here, we’re still just putting in the work and not feeling a need to leave the island. We’re just coming together and working hard. I’m happy with everything.” View this post on Instagram Source

item.title: The four factors that make Brighton genuine Premier League title contenders
item.description: When Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Brighton’s possible participation in the title race, he tended to invoke Getafe in his answer. And if a club from Madrid are not exactly an opponent in the Premier League, this was Hurzeler’s version of an old cliché. He is taking it one game at a time, and Brighton & Hove Albion ’s next game is against Getafe in the Europa Conference League . More pertinently, though, their last one was away at Manchester City . They defeated the league leaders . Brighton’s last week has served as a barometer of their status against the established powers. They played well against Liverpool at Anfield, but lost 2-0. They twice led against City in the Carabao Cup, but went out on penalties. They beat them in the Premier League. For a club with plenty of high-profile scalps in recent years, the Etihad Stadium was the final frontier. They had won everywhere else of note. Now Hurzeler could maintain the pretence that the only thing on his mind was Getafe. Brighton triumphed in Manchester in another impressive result for Fabian Hurzeler’s side (Getty) The unlikely challengers can deflect attention by citing the concerns they would have in other seasons. Eleven years ago, as Leicester City were an unexpected presence near the top of the table, Claudio Ranieri used to talk about targeting 40 points, even when it was clear Leicester would reach the usual barrier for safety with months to spare. Now Brighton are already halfway to the other mythical number, 38. Ranieri’s rhetoric was such that he could switch to meaningless but entertaining catchphrases; Hurzeler’s is less likely to spend spring saying “dilly ding, dilly dong”. But the subject of a title tilt could become inescapable if Brighton extend their superb start. That seems possible: they have played the rest of the current top five and do not face any again until the return game with City in January. They don’t see Chelsea again until April, Liverpool or Arsenal until the final two games. Leicester showed that an unlikely title triumph can be pulled off (PA Wire) Is there a title decider there? History would suggest not. Brighton have never finished in the top five of the top flight. They often start seasons well – they had 21 points after 12 games in 2024-25, 13 after six in 2022-23, 12 after five in 2021-22 – but have a past of winless spells, too: under Hurzeler, they twice went six league matches without victory last season. History suggests, too, that if Brighton are to upset the odds, it does not just depend upon their results. item.content:encoded: When Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Brighton’s possible participation in the title race, he tended to invoke Getafe in his answer. And if a club from Madrid are not exactly an opponent in the Premier League, this was Hurzeler’s version of an old cliché. He is taking it one game at a time, and Brighton & Hove Albion ’s next game is against Getafe in the Europa Conference League . More pertinently, though, their last one was away at Manchester City . They defeated the league leaders . Brighton’s last week has served as a barometer of their status against the established powers. They played well against Liverpool at Anfield, but lost 2-0. They twice led against City in the Carabao Cup, but went out on penalties. They beat them in the Premier League. For a club with plenty of high-profile scalps in recent years, the Etihad Stadium was the final frontier. They had won everywhere else of note. Now Hurzeler could maintain the pretence that the only thing on his mind was Getafe. Brighton triumphed in Manchester in another impressive result for Fabian Hurzeler’s side (Getty) The unlikely challengers can deflect attention by citing the concerns they would have in other seasons. Eleven years ago, as Leicester City were an unexpected presence near the top of the table, Claudio Ranieri used to talk about targeting 40 points, even when it was clear Leicester would reach the usual barrier for safety with months to spare. Now Brighton are already halfway to the other mythical number, 38. Ranieri’s rhetoric was such that he could switch to meaningless but entertaining catchphrases; Hurzeler’s is less likely to spend spring saying “dilly ding, dilly dong”. But the subject of a title tilt could become inescapable if Brighton extend their superb start. That seems possible: they have played the rest of the current top five and do not face any again until the return game with City in January. They don’t see Chelsea again until April, Liverpool or Arsenal until the final two games. Leicester showed that an unlikely title triumph can be pulled off (PA Wire) Is there a title decider there? History would suggest not. Brighton have never finished in the top five of the top flight. They often start seasons well – they had 21 points after 12 games in 2024-25, 13 after six in 2022-23, 12 after five in 2021-22 – but have a past of winless spells, too: under Hurzeler, they twice went six league matches without victory last season. History suggests, too, that if Brighton are to upset the odds, it does not just depend upon their results. When Leicester were champions in 2016, it was facilitated by the failures of others, as no one else secured more than 71 points. Ranieri’s team earned 81. Now some of the supposed superpowers, Manchester United in particular, seem to be taking themselves out of contention. A sizeable punishment could rule City out. It is altogether harder to see Arsenal, in particular, from ending up with under 80 points. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has built an excellent squad despite heavy turnover (PA Wire) Some elements indicate that Brighton should be taken seriously. One, oddly, lies in a couple of defeats: by losing their final two games of last season, they missed out on a Europa League spot. But the lighter load of the Conference League – both in its fixture list and lesser opponents – could equip them better for the Premier League. Another lies in the firepower of Hurzeler’s team. Brighton are the top scorers in the division. They are expert at sharing the goals around: 16 players have found the net in all competitions, 11 of them in the Premier League. It is all the more remarkable as they have been without last season’s first-choice front three, with Danny Welbeck gone to Chelsea and Yankuba Minteh and Kaoru Mitoma yet to play in the top flight this season. With Minteh fit again and the prospect of Mitoma being back next month, Brighton could have more devastating wingers. Brighton’s strong start has come despite being without last year’s front three (Getty) They have impressed defensively. They conceded four times to Chelsea, but only three other goals. Shutting City out gave them a sixth clean sheet of the season already, while they have only been breached once at home. Luka Vuskovic has been outstanding, submitting an early application for the title of signing of the season. But a test for players being introduced to such a physical and demanding division as the Croatian defender and the 21-year-old midfielder Chema Andres is whether they can sustain that form for a whole campaign. The same question can be applied to the team as a whole and to veterans like Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk. There are alternatives to each. The seeming strength of Brighton’s squad counts in their favour, even if it depends on Hurzeler continuing to pick the right option at the right time. Squad management will be key for Fabian Hurzeler and Brighton (Getty) But certainly, with Brighton already five points clear of sixth place and seven ahead of seventh, they are unlikely to get a better chance to qualify for the Champions League. Yet as they continue to be an indictment of the elite, selling their best players at premium prices, replacing them, and continuing to prosper, they are indulging in a unique experiment . Can a selling club win the world’s richest league? We may find out in May.

item.title: NFL Week 8 INSTANT reactions: Are the Cowboys cooked? Ravens need to make a move
item.description: Subscribe to Football 301 with Nate Tice Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Nate Tice & Hayden Winks dive into their instant takeaways from Week 8 of NFL action. The duo start with their takeaways from a sloppy Sunday night win for the Washington Commanders over the reeling Philadelphia Eagles. Nate & Hayden move on to their Pick 6 takeaways, featuring the Cincinnati Bengals winning a shootout with the Tennessee Titans, the Denver Broncos taking the AFC West lead over the Kansas City Chiefs, the Arizona Cardinals upsetting the Dallas Cowboys, the Detroit Lions beating the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beating the Atlanta Falcons without throwing a pass and the Pittsburgh Steelers shutting down the Cleveland Browns. The duo wrap up with a few Extra Credit items, including Lamar Jackson’s thumb injury and whether the Baltimore Ravens need to make a move for a quarterback, the Las Vegas Raiders & New York Jets lighting it up in a barn burner and the Jacksonville Jaguars crushing the Indianapolis Colts. item.title: Predators’ Chris MacFarland breaks silence on Shane Wright trade
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Predators’ Chris MacFarland breaks silence on Shane Wright trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Nashville Predators acquired Shane Wright in a trade with the Seattle Kraken on Sunday. This ends a bit of a saga within the Kraken. Wright has preferred a trade out of Seattle for a while now. He finally got his wish with this move. The newest Predators forward has had a rollercoaster of a career to this point. He was never able to establish himself as part of the Kraken’s core group of forwards. Nashville is excited to get a chance to work with him , as general manager Chris MacFarland explained on Sunday. “We are excited to add Shane to our mix of forwards,” the Predators GM said, via NHL.com. “We feel he will bring a strong, two-way game to our team and will add to the pace of our lineup… Shane will continue to grow as a player, and we look forward to working with him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Wright played nearly 170 games with Seattle prior to this trade. He scored 39 goals and 82 points in that time. The former fourth overall pick only has four points in 14 games this season. In return for Wright, the Predators sent young winger Matthew Wood to the Kraken. Wood, a former first-round pick, had just three points this season through 14 games. The 21-year-old scored 17 goals and 30 points during his first full NHL season in 2025-26. Wright finally has the fresh start he has sought for some time. What sort of impact he brings remains to be seen, but a fresh start inherently brings a new opportunity to thrive. The Predators return to the ice on Tuesday when they take on the Carolina Hurricanes. Related: Kraken, Predators swap forwards in intriguing midseason trade Related: Predators’ Barry Trotz drops Alex Ovechkin truth bomb amid final game in Nashville

item.title: Why Browns’ Todd Monken didn’t bench Deshaun Watson while Steelers teed off on him for 8 sacks in blowout
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Why Browns’ Todd Monken didn’t bench Deshaun Watson while Steelers teed off on him for 8 sacks in blowout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns endured a brutal afternoon against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Todd Monken’s decision to keep Deshaun Watson under center, though, revealed something about his approach to developing the offense. Despite watching his quarterback absorb eight sacks in Sunday’s embarrassing 27-6 defeat , the first-year head coach never seriously considered pulling him. Rather than turning to Shedeur Sanders, Monken wanted Watson to battle through adversity . Monken also accepted responsibility for the offensive breakdown. Through the first eight weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns have lived on a chaotic, razor-thin edge under first-year head coach Todd Monken . They have now compiled a 5-3 record that has showcased both incredible late-game resilience and glaring structural vulnerabilities. After bottoming out in a demoralizing 34-10 opening-day blowout in Jacksonville, Cleveland vaulted into playoff contention with five fourth-quarter comeback victories. Those were headlined by three walk-off field goals from Andre Szmyt against Pittsburgh, Baltimore, and Tennessee. However, their magic met a harsh reality check in Week 8 at Acrisure Stadium. This loss dropped Cleveland behind Pittsburgh in the AFC North. #Browns Todd Monken never considered taking Deshaun Watson out when the #Steelers were teeing off on him in the second half: pic.twitter.com/v9R6dqEzOd Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 1, 2026 According to Scott Petrak of The Chronicle-Telegram, Monken wanted Watson to accumulate more playing experience rather than remove him following the mounting pressure. “I want to see him play. I want to see him continue to play and battle,” Monken explained. He also refused to blame Watson alone, taking responsibility for the team’s preparation, offensive execution, and composure. “Everything starts with me,” Monken said, via Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com. The coach acknowledged that Cleveland must improve how it operates offensively and prepares as a team. With the Browns still sitting at 5-3, Monken clearly believes Watson needs opportunities to work through adversity rather than another quarterback change. Related: Browns’ Deshaun Watson refuses to blame O-Line despite getting shredded for 8 sacks vs. Steelers Related: Does Browns’ Jared Verse have regrets about Steelers trash talk? No freaking chance

item.title: Andy Reid Makes Muted Statement on Kingsley Suamataia After Second Benching
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on in the second quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: Kingsley Suamataia #76 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs made a surprise decision prior to the team’s loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday in benching left guard Kingsley Suamataia. The 2024 second round pick had already been benched in Week 4 in the win against the Las Vegas Raiders for unspecified reasons, and ahead of the team’s bout in Week 8 he did the very same thing. Andy Reid Comments on Kingsley Suamataia’s Benching Speaking to the media after the game, Reid declined to answer why he benched the third year offensive lineman. Andy Reid on Kingsley Suamataia: “It’s just between Kingsley and I.” — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) November 2, 2026 “It’s just between Kingsley and I,” Reid said after the loss when asked for the reasoning behind the decision. The first time the exact same situation arose the veteran head coach gave a similarly mute answer. #Chiefs HC Andy Reid on the surprise benching of starting LG Kingsley Suamataia 🗣️ “As far as the Kingsley thing goes before you guys ask, that’s between Kingsley and I, we’ll figure it out and down the road we’ll be better as a team for it and Kingsley will be better for it.” pic.twitter.com/ghaB9AVPsF — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) October 5, 2026 “As far as the Kingsley thing goes before you guys ask, that’s between Kingsley and I, we’ll figure it out and down the road we’ll be better as a team for it and Kingsley will be better for it.” Reid said after his benching in Week 4 back on Oct. 4. Kingsley Suamataia Second Benching Points to Ongoing Issues Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 02: Kingsley Suamataia #76 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) For the 68-year old to bench anyone is an uncommon occurrence for a head coach branded as anything but a disciplinarian. For him to do so twice in the first half of the season – and once again as a seemingly game-time decision would seem to imply that there is something very real going on behind the scenes. Especially as Reid explicitly noted that it was due to reasons concerning the two of them, rather a more generic answer arguing that 23-year old’s replacement, Mike Caliendo, was just the better option for the game. Andy Reid Comments on Kingsley Suamataia’s Benching Speaking to the media after the game, Reid declined to answer why he benched the third year offensive lineman. Andy Reid on Kingsley Suamataia: “It’s just between Kingsley and I.” — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) November 2, 2026 “It’s just between Kingsley and I,” Reid said after the loss when asked for the reasoning behind the decision. The first time the exact same situation arose the veteran head coach gave a similarly mute answer. #Chiefs HC Andy Reid on the surprise benching of starting LG Kingsley Suamataia 🗣️ “As far as the Kingsley thing goes before you guys ask, that’s between Kingsley and I, we’ll figure it out and down the road we’ll be better as a team for it and Kingsley will be better for it.” pic.twitter.com/ghaB9AVPsF — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) October 5, 2026 “As far as the Kingsley thing goes before you guys ask, that’s between Kingsley and I, we’ll figure it out and down the road we’ll be better as a team for it and Kingsley will be better for it.” Reid said after his benching in Week 4 back on Oct. 4. Kingsley Suamataia Second Benching Points to Ongoing Issues Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 02: Kingsley Suamataia #76 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) For the 68-year old to bench anyone is an uncommon occurrence for a head coach branded as anything but a disciplinarian. For him to do so twice in the first half of the season – and once again as a seemingly game-time decision would seem to imply that there is something very real going on behind the scenes. Especially as Reid explicitly noted that it was due to reasons concerning the two of them, rather a more generic answer arguing that 23-year old’s replacement, Mike Caliendo, was just the better option for the game. Perhaps this move could lead to the Chiefs taking further action this coming week as Kansas City prepares to take on the New York Jets . Even if it does not, the situation remains one of the more bizarre ongoing sagas in the KC locker room; and one that evidently requires a solution sooner rather than later. item.title: Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty
item.description: Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2-1 at San Mamés on Sunday 1 November to end their rivals' run of four straight league wins. The visitors have formally disputed the first-half penalty that decided the derby, while Athletic lost another striker to injury. Every goal in the Bilbao derby arrived before half-time. Nico Williams provided the assist for the opening goal. Luka Sučić equalised on the half-hour. A crowd of 50,092 watched the game. Before kick-off, Unai Simón presented his Yashin Trophy to the home crowd. A minute’s silence was also held for the victims of the Urda rail accident. Real Sociedad dispute the penalty that settled the derby The visitors left Bilbao angry about the decisive spot-kick. In its official match report, Real Sociedad called it a penalty that never was and criticised VAR for not stepping in. The club statement added that the chip inside the match ball shows Jon Aramburu made contact with the ball in his challenge on Nico Williams. Pellegrino Matarazzo said that for him it was clearly not a penalty. The Real Sociedad coach could not understand why VAR had not intervened to cancel it. He was booked for dissent in the 65th minute, a minute after Mamadou Sarr received a yellow card for the same offence. Referee Alejandro Hernandez showed Real Sociedad four yellow cards in total, against two for Athletic. The statistics point in two directions. Real Sociedad dominated the ball, completing 514 accurate passes to Athletic’s 307. Terzić’s side created the clearer chances, however. Unai Simón made four saves, while Álex Remiro made one. Sučić was the highest-rated player on the pitch at 7.52. Athletic win but lose another striker The victory came at a cost. Maroan Sannadi felt his hamstring early in the game. Athletic will need one or two more days to know how long he will be out. His injury follows Gorka Guruzeta’s serious knee injury at Valencia on 17 October, which left the squad short of strikers. With 83 minutes on the pitch, Navarro created four key passes and was rated 7.2. The win was Athletic’s third in a row across all competitions, after a 6-1 victory over Prat and a 4-0 win against Getafe. They sit seventh, two points behind Sevilla. Real Betis are four points clear of Real Sociedad. Athletic also have a game in hand. Their matchday-eight fixture at Rayo Vallecano was suspended. Objects landed on the field during that game, among them paper planes and tiny balls made of silicone. Rayo were fined €6,000, the maximum sanction under the disciplinary code. The match will resume behind closed doors at Vallecas on Wednesday 9 December at 20:00. Real Sociedad return to action first, hosting Lyon in the Europa League league phase on Thursday 5 November. Athletic travel to El Sadar to face Osasuna on matchday 12 on Saturday 7 November at 18:30. Sources Un penalti inexistente derrota a la Real (Real Sociedad) Este jueves se ponen a la ven

item.title: Eagles vs. Giants odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Tyrone Tracy Jr. #29 of the New York Giants carries the ball defended by Cooper DeJean #33 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles have lost six games in a row and the losing streak might continue next weekend. The Birds are three-point home underdogs to the New York Giants, according to FanDuel . As a reminder, the Eagles have NEVER won as home underdogs since Nick Sirianni was hired as head coach in 2021. They are 0-8 in those situations. Go Birds! Join Eagles fans on the SB Nation app! Share every touchdown celebration, big defensive stop and passionate game-day opinion with fellow Eagles fans. Join our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Jump easily between communities and conversations Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Eagles have longed owned the G-Men. But that might be changing. The Giants currently lead the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. And that’s despite the fact they lost their starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart, to a season-ending injury in Week 2. J.J. McCarthy is showing some promise with the Giants after previously being a bust for the Minnesota Vikings. John Harbaugh is going to have his team fired up to take on a reeling Eagles squad. The Giants also have a rest advantage in this matchup since they’re coming off their Week 8 bye while the Eagles are coming off a Sunday night road game. The Eagles aren’t inspiring any confidence at the moment. It’s impossible to give them the benefit of the doubt. What say you?

item.title: Julian Erosa Explains Retiring From UFC
item.description: Julian Erosa UFC Getty Long-time UFC featherweight fan favorite Julian Erosa explained why he made the decision to retire from mixed martial arts. Erosa laid down his gloves in the center of the Octagon following his first-round KO win over JeongYeong Lee at UFC Vegas 123, as he officially retired from the UFC with a final record of 10-9 inside the Octagon. Erosa had already announced before the fight that he was going to retire, so it wasn’t a surprise to see him hang up his gloves despite a terrific performance against Lee. So, why is Erosa retiring when he is seemingly still a UFC-caliber fighter? Julian Erosa Breaks Down Retirement Decision Speaking to reporters after UFC Vegas 123, Erosa broke down his decision to retire from MMA. “I was going back and forth in my mind: If I win the fight, I’m going to want to do it again because it’s the best feeling in the world. If I lose the fight, I’m going to want redemption. Win, lose or draw, I’m going to want to come back in here. So before I even got the fight, I told my wife, ‘This is going to be the last one,’ and be content with that decision. Once I was at ease with it and at peace with that decision, I could just go in the fight and just focus on it being a fight just like any other fight camp – focus on that and then be, I’m already happy with the decision of retiring. I didn’t want to be the guy that’s going to retire and then come back in a month. I’m happy with the way it turned out. I haven’t left any stone unturned. I made it from ‘Ultimate Fighter’ to Contender Series, been cut and rehired by the UFC so many times – I want to go out on my own terms,” Erosa said (via MMAjunkie.com ). Will Julian Erosa Compete Again? While Erosa did announce his retirement, it’s hard to take MMA fighters’ retirements at face value sometimes, as so many of them have hung up their gloves just to return a few years later. In Erosa’s case, it does feel like he’s done for good, as he has a young family to spend his time with. Not only that, but he was knocked out eight times in his career, so it is a smart decision to stop getting hit in the head anymore. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Julian Erosa Explains Retiring From UFC appeared first on HEAVY .
