item.title: Cowboys Could Cash Out on George Pickens ‘Subscription’ With Trade
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Of all the things that have gone wrong with the Dallas Cowboys thus far in what appears to be another cursed NFL season, the steady disappearance of wide receiver George Pickens is low down on the list. But that’s not because it’s unworthy of attention or scrutiny–it’s just because there are so many other issues to consider, so many other failures to address. The defense, the coaching, the indecisive approach to personnel, it all adds up to an incredibly disappointing 2026 season that started with the Cowboys openly talking about a trip to the Super Bowl, a bit of bravado that looks ridiculous in hindsight, like a gambler buying a lottery ticket certain that the millions are coming soon. It’s easy to lose Pickens in that shuffle. On Sunday, in the dramatic 33-30 loss to the Cardinals in overtime, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott targeted Pickens only four times, and Pickens played only about 40 snaps, around where he was in Week 7. A defensive meltdown was the reason the Cowboys collapsed on Sunday, but it is impossible to ignore the fact that the Cowboys are, well, ignoring Pickens. Cowboys Cutting George Pickens Snaps Why that’s happening is a fair question. Last week, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer publicly called out Pickens for his lack of seriousness when it comes to blocking in the run game. Pickens saw his snaps drop thereafter. But this is the same receiver who posted 93 catches and 1,429 yards last year, who was hailed for having the best training camp of any player on the Cowboys roster, and who was clearly focused on a big season that would lead to a big payout in free agency next winter. None of it has happened. The Cowboys have Pickens, and they’re not using him. Cleverly, Dallas Morning News writer Joseph Hoyt compared Pickens to, “a subscription that the Cowboys forgot they signed up for.” And Hoyt writes that the Cowboys, who have Pickens on a one-year, $27 million franchise tag contract, should dump Pickens and pick up whatever draft asset they can. The Cowboys treat George Pickens like a subscription they forgot they signed up for.It’s time to consider trading him before the deadline.Column: https://t.co/jYLODqtfql pic.twitter.com/mZqsCx9pxd — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) November 2, 2026 Trade Now, or Trade Later The Cowboys-George Pickens marriage clearly is not working. Hoyt suggests they should recognize that and explore what cashing out might bring. He wrote: “If the Cowboys were to trade Pickens then his new team couldn’t negotiate a long-term deal with him until after the season. That means a new team would be getting a receiver truly on an expiring contract, lowering the value of any potential midseason trade with Pickens. The Cowboys could wait until the offseason, tag Pickens again for a potential one-year deal worth more than $32 million, and then trade Pickens to a new destination … Would trading Pickens in a lost season for a Day 2 pick be worth it? Or is it better to wa

The Cowboys could wait until the offseason, tag Pickens again for a potential one-year deal worth more than $32 million, and then trade Pickens to a new destination … Would trading Pickens in a lost season for a Day 2 pick be worth it? Or is it better to wait to see what his market could be after the year?” Either way, Pickens would not be in the long-term plans of the Cowboys in either case. They’d be trading him–either after of the coming NFL deadline on November 10, or in the winter. But trading him nonetheless. That’s not where we thought this season, and relationship, was heading two months ago. item.title: What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse
item.description: Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Klint Kubiak and the Raiders got a much-needed win against the New York Jets in Week 8 that saw Brock Bowers set a mark not seen since 2016 . Ashton Jeanty called out the Jets before the game and was asked about his comments, taking the high road as his team turned to Mike Washington Jr. as its leading ballcarrier. Kubiak’s comments were shared by Sam Gordon of the Las Vegas Review Journal, during which he addressed the Jeanty situation. “Yeah, you know guys, that’s my call, and Ashton’s still gonna be a big part of our team. Had a huge catch, he’s gonna be a huge part of our run game going forward, and, you know, we just wanna give Mike a few more opportunities a day, and, you know, I think both guys are going to be a huge part of our rushing and passing success moving forward.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kubiak replied “no” when asked if Jeanty’s comments on the Jets had anything to do with his lack of carries on the day. Washington Jr. did well with 25 carries for 83 yards while Jeanty was a factor in the passing game with three catches for 64 yards. QB Kirk Cousins focused on Jeanty along with tight ends Bowers and Michael Mayer in the passing game as the Raiders beat a struggling NY team. Rex Ryan called out Jeanty after his comments on the Jets, showing that the Raiders still have the ability to move the dial on a national level. Fans care about the Raiders from coast-to-coast, and Jeanty is a big reason why. He’s an exciting running back who will get another chance to shine in the near future as the Raiders’ train rolls on. Related: Raiders news: Only 1 thing surprises Klint Kubiak about Brock Bowers after another big day Related: Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets

item.title: ‘Kirk Cousins, Come Home to Minnesota’ — Ex-NFL QB Pushes Vikings to ‘Secretly’ Consider Trade for Raiders Star And Replace Kyler Murray
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Minnesota Vikings moved on from Kirk Cousins, traded J.J. McCarthy, and handed Kyler Murray the starting job. Now, Minnesota has a quarterback problem that makes those decisions harder to ignore. Murray has yet to give the offense the level of play it needs, while Cousins is putting together strong performances in Las Vegas, in a turn of events that has former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel wondering why the Vikings have not quietly explored bringing their former starter back. Chase Daniel Urges Vikings to Explore Kirk Cousins Trade Speaking on “Bussin’ With The Boys” after Week 8, Daniel argued that Minnesota should not rely entirely on its defense while Murray works through his uneven performances. He believes the Vikings need to consider bringing Cousins back from the Las Vegas Raiders, especially after the veteran’s recent outing against the New York Jets. “If you are the Vikings, you need to be back in the race and back in the thought of absolutely looking into Kirk Cousins. Why are you not secretly checking into the Raiders and Kirk Cousins? Kirk is absolutely balling and had an amazing game versus the Jets. Your defense cannot carry you the entire year,” Daniel said. Cousins, who ranks 10th in PFN’s NFL QB Impact Metric , has given Daniel a reason to raise the possibility. Against New York, he completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in a 38-33 victory. He also scored a rushing touchdown, finishing with a 141.0 passer rating. His previous two appearances included 295 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams, following 313 yards and two touchdowns against Buffalo. item.title: 🟥 Juve-Napoli, press: Koop deserved red after 10'! Lucumi too, review 📺
item.description: 🟥 Juve-Napoli, press: Koop deserved red after 10'! Lucumi too, review 📺 Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 in Sunday's big Serie A clash between two of the biggest disappointments of the season so far. Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! At the Allianz Stadium, superb goals from Alajbegovic and Boga , both in the second half, proved decisive after a largely uneventful opening period. Everything, however, could have changed after just ten minutes, when Koopmeiners brought down Anguissa with a nasty challenge . Even as it happened, DAZN 's co-commentator suggested VAR might intervene, but no call came. Referee Sozza then allowed play to resume without even booking the Dutchman . 😳 Newspapers in no doubt: it was a red! A wrong decision, judging by the comments in today's newspapers. Both Gazzetta dello Sport and Corriere dello Sport felt the Dutchman's foul warranted a sending-off. Gazzetta gives Sozza a rating of 4.5 , adding that " as early as the eighth minute, he fails to book McKennie. In the 11th, he doesn't even book Koopmeiners: a challenge halfway up Anguissa's leg that constitutes serious foul play, clearly dangerous — it should have been a red ". Corriere , meanwhile, rates the referee's performance a 5 : " Sozza's performance was far from spotless — quite the opposite: the opening quarter of an hour was a nightmare (even though Halloween was over), and the Koopmeiners decision hangs over the match. A late challenge, with a straight leg and studs showing: true, it wasn't a 'lunge' but a 'scrape', which gives those arguing his innocence some room for manoeuvre, but going from a possible red to not even awarding a foul (and a yellow) means an error on the pitch and confusion in his head ". For former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese , however, "a red would have been excessive . But if Sozza had shown one, I don't think VAR would have intervened". According to Corriere, there could also have been another sending-off : " Speaking of risking a red: Lucumi takes a big risk when, already on a booking, he makes a clumsy challenge on Lucca. A second yellow would have been justified ". This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇮🇹 here.

item.title: Travis Kelce Has Strong Words on Andy Reid After Chiefs’ Loss to Broncos
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce sends a clear message on head coach Andy Reid after losing to the Broncos. Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce runs the ball against the Broncos in Week 8. Getty Head coach Andy Reid and Travis Kelce Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce takes responsibility for his role in the team's performance over the past few weeks. Getty The Kansas City Chiefs took their second consecutive loss of the season against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. During the 28-24 loss, the Chiefs got hit with 11 penalties for 105 yards. Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who caught five receptions for 62 yards against Denver, spoke to reporters after Kansas City fell to second place in the AFC West. “We got a lot of fight,” he said. “You got to take the positives out of this. You can’t dwell on it. They’re a pretty good football team,” Kelce said of the Broncos, a team they crushed 31-10 in Week 1. Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce runs the ball against the Broncos in Week 8. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid faced criticism for his questionable play calls against the Broncos, like sending out a struggling Harrison Butker to kick a 54-yard field goal in the rain on 4th and eight. His mysterious decision to keep left guard Kingsley Suamataia on the bench also left fans perplexed. After the game, Kelce shared a strong message about Reid. Travis Kelce Says It’s Their Job to Make Chiefs Head Coach Andy Reid’s Plays Work While Kelce wants to see the film “and see what the answers are and how we can get better from it,” the 37-year-old made it clear that the fault is in their execution, not Reid’s play calls. Getty Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has the full support from tight end Travis Kelce. “There’s a mentality that whatever Coach Reid calls, you got to find a way to get it into the end zone,” he said. “And that’s the bottom line . That’s the mentality. And from here on out, it’s gotta be how we roll. And we have to execute.” Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is on the same page. “Yeah, obviously penalties, some miscommunications between me and the receivers and running backs and stuff like that,” Mahomes told reporters. “Just in general, the execution wasn’t at a high enough level.” “We made big plays, and we made plays happen against a really good defense. But whenever you’re playing a team like that in the division, you’ve got to execute for the full 60 minutes, and we weren’t able to do that.” As for Sumataia’s benching, Kelce said he loves the guy and is “not sure what the scenario” is there. item.title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley doesn’t hold back on Philadelphia’s free fall
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Eagles RB Saquon Barkley doesn’t hold back on Philadelphia’s free fall appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles ’ losing streak keeps growing after a loss to the Washington Commander s, and Saquon Barkley is not sugarcoating how it feels. After Philadelphia fell 27-10 on Sunday Night Football , the star running back gave a blunt assessment of where the team stands. “This one sucks. They all suck,” Barkley said, via Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. “The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we’ve got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Saquon Barkley: "This one sucks. They all suck. The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we've got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat. "We've got to lock in, fast." pic.twitter.com/DL1rDJNQcw — Olivia Reiner (@ReinerOlivia) November 2, 2026 Barkley added, “We’ve got to lock in, fast.” The defeat was the Eagles’ sixth straight, dropping them to 2-6 on the season . It started well enough at Northwest Stadium. Jake Elliott opened the scoring with a 40-yard field goal, and Barkley took a direct snap and punched in a 3-yard touchdown run to give Philadelphia a 10-0 lead in the first quarter. The Eagles did not score again. Washington answered with 27 unanswered points, as Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Commanders added four field goals, including a 56-yarder. A 1-yard touchdown run and a two-point conversion with 1:55 left capped the scoring. The win improved Washington to 2-4-1 and marked its first comeback victory of the season. Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown without an interception, while the Commanders’ defense sacked Tanner McKee five times. McKee, filling in for the injured Jalen Hurts, went 23-of-34 for 212 yards with an interception. Barkley, who entered the week dealing with hamstring and back injuries, was held to 30 yards on 13 carries. He added a 24-yard catch out of the backfield. Elijah Mitchell, elevated from the practice squad on Saturday , also got 11 carries. The 29-year-old is not the only Eagle taking accountability during the skid. Last week, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took the blame after the Dallas Cowboys ran for 204 yards in a 38-21 loss on Monday Night Football. The good news for Philadelphia is that the NFC East remains up for grabs. The New York Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, and the Eagles will host them at Lincoln Financial Field next Sunday. If Philadelphia hopes to salvage its season, the turnaround will need to start there. Related: Eagles’ Nick Sirianni puts himself on blast after Week 8 SNF debacle vs. Commanders Related: Eagles’ Nick Sirianni doesn’t give a clear answer on Sean Mannion’s playcalling duties

item.title: “He Is Washed Up,” “Not a Top 5 QB Anymore”: NFL Fans Rip Patrick Mahomes After Costly Error Leads to Chiefs’ Loss vs. Broncos
item.description: Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) reacts during the second half against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium. © Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Patrick Mahomes is facing the heat after making a costly mistake that cost the Kansas City Chiefs the game in Sunday’s 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. Andy Reid and his team led 24-21. During a third-and-2 with 2:44 left, the three-time Super Bowl champion tried to find space in the pocket to make a pass. Mahomes ran to the right before being sacked by linebacker Alex Singleton , resulting in a 6-yard loss. Harrison Butker then came on for a 54-yard field-goal attempt. However, he missed, and possession changed hands. The Broncos then set up running back Jonah Coleman for a 5-yard rushing TD, which put Sean Payton and his team ahead for good. Fans on social media did not shy away from criticizing Patrick Mahomes for the costly sack. “Patrick Mahomes is not a top 5 QB anymore. He may not be top 10,” one fan commented. “Chiefs about to lose because Patrick Mahomes took an idiotic sack. That brother is washed up,” another fan said. Here are more reactions: With a few seconds left in the game, it looked like the Chiefs (5-2) scored a go-ahead touchdown to win the game. However, Jaylon Moore was flagged for a false start, nullifying the play. On fourth-and-goal, Patrick Mahomes ended up being sacked by defensive tackle Malcolm Roach as time expired. The three-time Super Bowl champion completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three TDs. Patrick Mahomes expresses disappointment after Sunday’s loss to the Denver Broncos In the postgame news conference, Patrick Mahomes admitted that the Kansas City Chiefs made a lot of mistakes that cost them the game. “We just made too many mistakes,” Mahomes said. “When you make mistakes, you’re going to lose against good football teams.” The quarterback also vowed to improve despite the loss to the Denver Broncos. “Obviously it’s a big game, I’m not going to hide from that, but now you’re in a dogfight for the division. I was proud of how the guys battled; it wasn’t perfect, but we battled. We’ll learn from it.” The Chiefs are next scheduled to face the New York Jets on Sunday. He may not be top 10,” one fan commented. “Chiefs about to lose because Patrick Mahomes took an idiotic sack. That brother is washed up,” another fan said. Here are more reactions: With a few seconds left in the game, it looked like the Chiefs (5-2) scored a go-ahead touchdown to win the game. However, Jaylon Moore was flagged for a false start, nullifying the play. On fourth-and-goal, Patrick Mahomes ended up being sacked by defensive tackle Malcolm Roach as time expired. The three-time Super Bowl champion completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three TDs. Patrick Mahomes expresses disappointment after Sunday’s loss to the Denver Broncos In the postgame news conference, Patrick Mahomes admitted that the Kansas City Chiefs made a lot of mistakes that cost them the game. “We just made too many mistakes,” Mahomes said. “When you make mistakes, you’re going to lose against good football teams.” The quarterback also vowed to improve despite the loss to the Denver Broncos. “Obviously it’s a big game, I’m not going to hide from that, but now you’re in a dogfight for the division. I was proud of how the guys battled; it wasn’t perfect, but we battled. We’ll learn from it.” The Chiefs are next scheduled to face the New York Jets on Sunday. item.title: ‘Advantage In Every Area’ – Lucas Gabriel Aims To End Magomed Magomedov’s Unbeaten Run At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Lucas Gabriel steps into his first main event on martial arts’ grandest stage, and he plans to make the most of the moment. He faces undefeated promotional newcomer Magomed “Muhammad” Magomedov in a lightweight MMA showdown at ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video , which goes down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6. Photo Credit: ONE Championship His opponent, however, was never part of the original plan. The Brazilian had spent his camp preparing for former ONE Lightweight MMA World Title challenger Alibeg Rasulov , until an injury forced the Turkish star off the card. Magomedov – a perfect 15-0 in his career – answered on short notice. A swap this close to fight night can tilt a camp off its axis, but Gabriel’s blueprint has stayed intact. Gabriel told onefc.com: “He has a similar style to my previous opponent, so I haven’t had to change much since the fight was switched. I know he’s an undefeated and well-rounded fighter.” View this post on Instagram While the Phuket Fight Club affiliate respects Magomedov’s credentials , he expects the Dagestani to stay true to his roots, and he is ready to meet him there. A Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt with heavy hands to match, Gabriel can end a fight from anywhere, and he has a firm read on how this one unfolds. The 26-year-old said: “He tends to rely more on grappling, which often leaves openings in his stand-up game. I believe I have the advantage in every area. My jiu-jitsu is much better, and I also believe my striking is superior.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Gabriel sounds certain he is a step ahead wherever this fight goes, and he plans to prove it with a finish. A seventh straight appearance without defeat in the world’s largest martial arts organization is the goal, and he wants it to arrive with an ending the highlight reels will replay. item.title: 'The Sea God Surveys': Watch Rocket Lab launch Japanese Earth-observing satellite today
item.description: null Rocket Lab will launch its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site today, during a window that opens at 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT; 5:30 a.m. on Nov. 3 local New Zealand time), The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Sea God Surveys," will carry an Earth-observing radar satellite for the Japanese company iQPS. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before launch, and Space.com will carry the company's feed if, as expected, it's made available. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Sea God Surveys" mission, which is expected to launch on Nov. 2, 2025. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Sea God Surveys" will be Rocket Lab's 10th launch to date for iQPS, which is assembling a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). SAR satellites offer advantages over those that view our planet in optical wavelengths. They can peer through cloud cover, for example, and study our planet at night as well as during the day. Today's launch will be the 99th overall for Rocket Lab and the 90th for the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron, which gives small satellites dedicated rides to space. The workhorse vehicle has already flown 16 times this year. Rocket Lab's other nine launches to date have been conducted by HASTE , a suborbital version of Electron that allows customers to test their tech in the hypersonic flight environment. HASTE (short for "Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron") debuted in June 2023 and generally flies classified payloads.

item.title: Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2 trn in October
item.description: …As investors reap N4.5trn WoW By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market strengthened Month-on-Month (MoM), in October 2026, as renewed buying interest in heavyweight stocks lifted the benchmark of the Nigerian Exchange, NGX Index above the 250,000-point psychological threshold. The rally added N2.01 trillion to market capitalisation, reflecting strong price appreciation in selected large-capitalised stocks across the Industrial Goods, Financial Services and Energy sectors. According to analysts, although the market’s upward movement suggests renewed investor confidence, the uneven distribution of gains points to a selective investment strategy. Investors appear to be concentrating on stocks with significant market influence while maintaining a cautious approach towards other equities. This divergence between index performance and market breadth remains an important consideration in assessing the sustainability of the current rally. Specifically, breakdown of trading in October showed that the NGX market capitalisation closed at N165.114 trillion from 163.104 trillion in September. Similarly, the NGX All Share Index, ASI surged by 1.2% to close at 254,299.49 points from 251,211.67 points in September. Meanwhile on Week-on-Week, WoW the market gained N4.595 trillion as market capitalisation rose from N160.519 trillion the previous week in October to close at N165.114 trillion last week while the NGX ASI rose by 2.9% from 247,222.27 points previous week to close at 254,299.49 points last week. On the global market, the oil prices continued to record performance as the retreat in prices last week reflected a reassessment of geopolitical risks as diplomatic efforts sought to revive peace negotiations. However, analysts noted that the outlook for oil remains sensitive to developments in the region, and renewed escalation could quickly alter market expectations. For Nigeria, movements in crude oil prices have implications for government revenue, foreign exchange supply and broader economic expectations. Higher oil prices can support public revenue and external balances, although their overall effect depends on production levels, domestic fuel costs and other economic conditions. Lower oil prices may ease some cost pressures but could also weaken revenue expectations if the decline is sustained. The effect on listed companies will vary according to their exposure to energy prices, foreign exchange movements, production costs and domestic demand. On market outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited stated: “Investors should therefore consider international oil movements alongside domestic economic indicators and company-specific developments rather than treating changes in crude prices as a uniform signal for the entire equities market. ‘‘More broadly, expectations regarding interest rates, inflation, corporate earnings and foreign exchange conditions may influence portfolio allocation decisions. ‘‘Where investors anticipate improved corporate p

item.title: Dangerous spices: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
item.description: By Elizabet Adegbesan For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable. But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector. Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags. The cost of a crunch The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal. The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years. For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating. “If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away. “People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.” The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil. As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell. Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks. A lifestyle of hustle and denial In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation. The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary. With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred. Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product. “The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. “If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch. “I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.” For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly. Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health. The regulatory blind spot Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives. However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible. Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable. item.title: Chap who coded Google’s Pac-Man clone reveals how the game freaked out Firefox
item.description: A designer named Marcin Wichary has revealed the story of how he freaked out a decent slab of the world’s Firefox-using population with Pac-Man. Wichary has held senior design roles at Figma, Medium, and Google. As he wrote here , in 2010 Google decided to celebrate the 30 th anniversary of Pac-Man by changing its logo at Google.com to a playable version of the game. The Google of 2010 could still mention its motto of the time, “Don’t be evil,” without making anyone who heard it guffaw incredulously. The company’s frequent changes to the logo on its homepage – called Google Doodles , and which persist to this day – were still a notable part of net culture. Wichary got the job of building the playable logo, and tweaking Pac-Man to replace its usual maze with a course that instead navigated around the letters GOOGLE. “It was, frankly, a terrifying proposition,” Wichary wrote. “The homepage was then a very important destination, and my job title was only adjacent to ‘software engineer.’ But I started researching the game and recreating it all in HTML and CSS." Google wanted a full Pac-Man experience, including sound, "because so many of Pac-Man’s sounds are beyond iconic: the starting melody, the waka-wakas, the death jingle." Wichary began work before Google sought permission from Pac-Man’s owner Namco, because the search giant was “planning to wow them with a close-to-finished doodle.” “The project was … going really well. I had fun coding the game and we seemed to have fun playing it. Namco eventually got onboard, too,” he wrote. Those people used the Firefox browser with an extension called CoolPreviews that let users hover over a link to see a preview of a web page. “The extension would quietly start at the same time Firefox was opened,” Wichary explained. “And it would immediately, in the background, invisibly and unbeknownst to the user, open a website.” That website was Google’s home page, which now featured an auto-playing and version of Pac-Man that CoolPreviews users simply did not expect. item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: A designer named Marcin Wichary has revealed the story of how he freaked out a decent slab of the world’s Firefox-using population with Pac-Man. Wichary has held senior design roles at Figma, Medium, and Google. As he wrote here , in 2010 Google decided to celebrate the 30 th anniversary of Pac-Man by changing its logo at Google.com to a playable version of the game. The Google of 2010 could still mention its motto of the time, “Don’t be evil,” without making anyone who heard it guffaw incredulously. The company’s frequent changes to the logo on its homepage – called Google Doodles , and which persist to this day – were still a notable part of net culture. Wichary got the job of building the playable logo, and tweaking Pac-Man to replace its usual maze with a course that instead navigated around the letters GOOGLE. “It was, frankly, a terrifying proposition,” Wichary wrote. “The homepage was then a very important destination, and my job title was only adjacent to ‘software engineer.’ But I started researching the game and recreating it all in HTML and CSS." Google wanted a full Pac-Man experience, including sound, "because so many of Pac-Man’s sounds are beyond iconic: the starting melody, the waka-wakas, the death jingle." Wichary began work before Google sought permission from Pac-Man’s owner Namco, because the search giant was “planning to wow them with a close-to-finished doodle.” “The project was … going really well. I had fun coding the game and we seemed to have fun playing it. Namco eventually got onboard, too,” he wrote. Google liked the game work so much, higher-ups decided it would be a great idea to have it start automatically if visitors to google.com stayed idle for ten seconds. The designer liked that idea. “If there was anything scary about it at the time, it was only the thought of my code getting even more exposure – but I wasn’t worried about distraction, since the homepage was not a destination page you would ever linger on.” What Google didn’t realise was that some people lingered on the home page without ever knowing they were there. Those people used the Firefox browser with an extension called CoolPreviews that let users hover over a link to see a preview of a web page. “The extension would quietly start at the same time Firefox was opened,” Wichary explained. “And it would immediately, in the background, invisibly and unbeknownst to the user, open a website.” That website was Google’s home page, which now featured an auto-playing and version of Pac-Man that CoolPreviews users simply did not expect. Which explained why, not long after setting the Pac-Man doodle live, Google received plenty of praise, but also reports about computers making strange noises due to CoolPreviews invisibly opening the noisy game. “I pushed a patch within hours,” Wichary wrote, explaining that he added a mute button and a requirement to click something to make the game and its noises start. CoolPreviews couldn’t make those clicks, so the phantom Pac-Man sounds went away. “Ironically, I don’t believe we ever heard of normal people being bothered by the autoplay – it seemed that indeed, few people stayed on the homepage for 10 seconds doing absolutely nothing,” Wichary wrote. “The funny thing is that emergency live-patching [the] internet’s at the time most valuable homepage was perhaps the scariest part of that day for me, but that completely went over my sleep-deprived head,” he added. Google changed Wichary’s title after this incident. His post shows an image describing him as “User experience designer. The Michael Bay of doodles.” ®

item.title: Monarch’s murder: Nwifuru seeks death penalty for kidnappers
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo Ebonyi State Government has forwarded an executive bill to the State House of Assembly seeking to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment. Governor Francis Nwifuru disclosed this at the weekend during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike autonomous community in Ikwo Local Government Area, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Eric Igwe, was abducted on Sunday, March 1, while on his way to church. He was reportedly killed by his abductors a day after. Speaking at the funeral, conducted by the Assemblies of God Church, Nwifuru lamented what he described as the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths, expressing concern about their readiness to assume leadership positions in the future. He also pledged to implement any court decision against those arrested over the monarch’s murder, adding that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping and abduction in the state. The governor said: “I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally. “I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths. “The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders. They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.” He warned that the monarch’s murder should be the last such incident in Ikwo and other parts of the state. “I will not wait to execute the decision of the court over the murderers of this monarch, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. We have sent a bill to the House of Assembly to make kidnapping attract the death sentence by hanging in the state, with no other option. This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnap, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said. Nwifuru described the late monarch as a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State and attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians. In tributes, former governors Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Anyim Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies. They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society. In his tribute, the monarch’s first son, Igwe, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture. item.title: itel Energy offers 48-hour repairs, product replacement to customers at exhibition
item.description: itel Energy, a clean energy and power solutions brand, has promised to repair or replace faulty solar power equipment within 48 hours for customers across Nigeria as part of its after-sales support. The company reemphasized their commitment during the Nigeria Energy exhibition week in Lagos, where it showcased new products and showed distributors, installers, both new and existing customers how its after-sales service works. The company said it offers remote services, home visits and product replacement where necessary. According to the company, after-sales service is an important consideration for households and businesses switching from petrol and diesel generators to solar power, because a faulty inverter or battery can disrupt electricity supply and business operations. Speaking on the sidelines at the exhibition, the Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of SunFi, a major distributor of itel Energy products, Rotimi Thomas, said the commitment boosted customers’ confidence in the products distributed through the company. “The 48-hour resolution commitment from itel Energy is very important for us as a distribution platform because we don’t make the product and when a consumer buys a product through SunFi, they’re actually really buying a trusted service,” Thomas said. He explained that customers needed assurance that equipment would be repaired or replaced when problems arose, rather than being left to deal with faults after purchase. “That trust comes from the type of equipment that we use and the promise of being able to replace or repair the assets when there’s a problem,” he said. Thomas also urged customers to look beyond warranty periods when choosing solar equipment, saying the speed and quality of support during the warranty period were equally important. “But even more important than that five-year warranty is what happens before the five years or during the five-year period. How do you respond when I report that I have a problem with the product now?” Thomas said the cost of solar systems remained a barrier to adoption, adding that the company offers instalment payment plans for households and businesses unable to pay the full amount. According to him, about 30 to 40 per cent of prospective customers still request payment plans, which shows the need for financing options that make clean energy more accessible. He said some customers preferred to pay between 10 and 30 per cent upfront and spread the balance over three, six, 12 or 24 months, or longer. Meanwhile, itel Energy’s Country Service Manager, Emmanuel Kumuyi, said most common complaints reported by customers included overloading, protection issues and incorrect installation. He said some problems arose when solar panels, inverters and batteries were not properly matched to the user’s power requirements. According to him, about 30 to 40 per cent of prospective customers still request payment plans, which shows the need for financing options that make clean energy more accessible. He said some customers preferred to pay between 10 and 30 per cent upfront and spread the balance over three, six, 12 or 24 months, or longer. Meanwhile, itel Energy’s Country Service Manager, Emmanuel Kumuyi, said most common complaints reported by customers included overloading, protection issues and incorrect installation. He said some problems arose when solar panels, inverters and batteries were not properly matched to the user’s power requirements. Kumuyi advised customers to use certified engineers for installation and to ensure that their systems were correctly configured. He explained that when a customer reports a fault, the company’s service agents document the complaint and refer it to an engineer for remote assistance. According to him, if the problem cannot be resolved remotely, an engineer is assigned to visit the customer’s premises. Where necessary, component or product replacement is initiated in line with the applicable warranty terms. The company’s National Distributor Manager, Lucky Ovenseri, said itel Energy had distribution coverage across Nigeria’s 36 states, with showrooms and dedicated energy after-sales centres in major cities, including Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan and Kano. He said the company also operated a replacement policy under which customers could receive another unit while their faulty equipment was being handled. At the exhibition, itel Energy showcased its newly launched PowerTank 1000 and IP54 11kW Hybrid Inverter, targeting customers with different electricity needs. The PowerTank 1000 demonstration featured a powered mini-chiller and a water dispenser, while visitors interested in the 11kW hybrid inverter sought information about pricing, installation, warranty coverage and its ability to support higher power demands. The company currently has 5 Flagship service centers, and over 200 service centers across more than 60 cities, backed by Carlcare and Transsion Group’s network of 2,000+ service centers spread across Sub-saharan Africa,Middle-East,and Asia. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 2, 2026
item.description: The naira’s exchange rate against the US dollar remains a major focus for businesses, importers, investors and Nigerians who depend on foreign currency for international transactions. The Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market are two major segments of Nigeria’s foreign exchange market, with rates varying according to currency supply, demand and market conditions. As of Monday, November 2, 2026, the latest available figures indicate that the official NFEM rate stood at ₦1,346.26 per dollar, while the parallel market quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,386.36. Official NFEM exchange rate Data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the naira traded at an average rate of ₦1,346.2565 per dollar on Friday, October 30, the latest available official trading data ahead of Monday’s session. The official market also recorded a closing rate of ₦1,346.00 per dollar, reflecting a marginal improvement from the previous trading session. The NFEM rate is determined by the volume-weighted average of transactions in the official foreign exchange market. It serves as the benchmark for official foreign currency transactions in Nigeria. Central Bank of Nigeria Dollar to naira black market rate today In the parallel market, commonly known as the black market, currency dealers quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,380.59 for buying and ₦1,386.36 for selling as of Sunday, November 1. This means Nigerians seeking to purchase one dollar from parallel market operators would need approximately ₦1,386, although the actual amount may vary depending on the dealer and location. The parallel market rates are indicative and may change throughout the day in response to foreign exchange demand and supply. Difference between official and parallel market rates The difference between the latest official NFEM weighted average of ₦1,346.26 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36 is approximately ₦40.10 per dollar. The gap reflects differences in foreign exchange supply, demand and pricing across the two markets. For individuals and businesses purchasing dollars, the parallel market selling rate remains an important consideration, particularly for transactions that cannot be processed through official banking channels. How much is $100 in naira today? At the latest available official NFEM rate of ₦1,346.26, $100 is equivalent to approximately ₦134,626. At the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36, $100 would cost approximately ₦138,636. These figures are indicative and do not necessarily represent the final rates offered by banks or individual currency dealers. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing exchange rates with their banks or licensed Bureau de Change operators before conducting foreign exchange transactions. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 2, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I confronted religious merchants in Kaduna to achieve peace — Uba Sani
item.description: By Charles Kumolu For years, Kaduna State was synonymous with ethno-religious violence, communal distrust, and bloodshed, with successive administrations struggling to end the cycle of killings that fractured communities and undermined the state’s economic and social life. But Governor Uba Sani believes the tide has turned, insisting that the peace being experienced in the state is the product of deliberate efforts to dismantle what he calls the “merchants of ethno-religious crises,” promote inclusive governance, and address the economic conditions that fuel insecurity. From Southern Kaduna to Birnin Gwari, he says, the emphasis has been on rebuilding trust, taking development to neglected communities, and making citizens see one another as partners rather than adversaries. In this interview with a team of editors from Vanguard Newspapers, the governor explains the thinking behind his Kaduna Model, how his administration secured the release of 222 captives in Birnin Gwari through the reopening of markets, and why he believes economic empowerment is central to sustainable peace. He also responds to allegations of intolerance toward opposition politicians, speaks on the role of political elites in exploiting ethnic and religious divisions, and outlines his administration’s efforts to reposition Kaduna through agriculture, rural roads, transportation, and sports infrastructure. In Rivers State’s history, it was once known as Rivers of Blood. About 10 years ago, Kaduna was known as a state of blood, crisis, and bloodshed. How were you able to restore peace, especially in Southern Kaduna? When we came in, the first thing we looked at was recognising the fact that our state is the most diverse state in Nigeria. Of course, I agree with you that the number of lives we lost in Kaduna in the last 20 years, before we came, was more than the number of lives lost because of insurgency, kidnapping, and banditry. Knowing that, we believed that for us to claim any success as a government, we must bring our people together. The only way we could do that was by ensuring that we created a state where everyone would be carried along in whatever we were doing. In this interview with a team of editors from Vanguard Newspapers, the governor explains the thinking behind his Kaduna Model, how his administration secured the release of 222 captives in Birnin Gwari through the reopening of markets, and why he believes economic empowerment is central to sustainable peace. He also responds to allegations of intolerance toward opposition politicians, speaks on the role of political elites in exploiting ethnic and religious divisions, and outlines his administration’s efforts to reposition Kaduna through agriculture, rural roads, transportation, and sports infrastructure. In Rivers State’s history, it was once known as Rivers of Blood. About 10 years ago, Kaduna was known as a state of blood, crisis, and bloodshed. How were you able to restore peace, especially in Southern Kaduna? When we came in, the first thing we looked at was recognising the fact that our state is the most diverse state in Nigeria. Of course, I agree with you that the number of lives we lost in Kaduna in the last 20 years, before we came, was more than the number of lives lost because of insurgency, kidnapping, and banditry. Knowing that, we believed that for us to claim any success as a government, we must bring our people together. The only way we could do that was by ensuring that we created a state where everyone would be carried along in whatever we were doing. Of course, we decided to run a system that would bring everyone together, which is a highly inclusive government. For us, inclusivity isn’t just about bringing people to sit with us. It’s about taking development to every part of Kaduna State. When we came in, we looked at the deficits in terms of infrastructure, healthcare, and education. We looked at this holistically, and we believed it was the only way we could address injustice and marginalisation. Some people felt they were not treated like citizens of our state. We believed that doing that really demanded that we relegate politics and elevate governance. Doing that, of course, could sometimes be difficult because when you are elected as a governor, you have people who work with you. The first thing they tell you is to consider people who voted for you and ignore those who did not. But when we came in, it was not about who voted for us and who did not; it wasn’t the issue at all. It was about carrying everyone along. So, we really tried to put that aside and focus on carrying everyone along, including those who did not vote for us. We took development to every part of Kaduna State, irrespective of party, religious, or ethnic affiliation. Of course, a lot of people have been talking about the Kaduna Model, asking how we did it. That is because in the last three and a half years in Kaduna, we have not experienced a single ethno-religious crisis, which is highly unprecedented. But for me, the Kaduna Model is nothing difficult. It’s about running a state where you carry everyone along and, as much as possible, be fair to everyone. Of course, human beings want justice. Sometimes you might work with people who are certainly merchants. When I say merchants, I mean people who only survive whenever there is an ethno-religious crisis. You have to eliminate them within the system. If you don’t eliminate them within the system, the problem will continue. We tried as much as possible to eliminate those merchants, which was actually very difficult. That was because some of them also felt they were part of the system, and they also helped to win the election. That was the first battle you have to encounter as a leader. Did you say merchants? Yes, ethno-religious merchants. For me, it takes a lot of political will to do that because they also feel they have a stake. Probably some of them contributed significantly to making one win the election. But then, along that line, of course, I had issues with many people who probably misunderstood my ideology. I tried to explain to some that they need to go back. Happily, I look at my antecedents. I am not just a normal politician. I’m someone who spent many years fighting for justice, equality, democracy, and the rule of law. So, putting my ideology aside is very difficult. I paid my dues. I went to detention five times fighting for democracy in Nigeria. I was in the Senate. I would have been comfortable. But I decided to contest for the governorship of my state simply because I wasn’t happy about how toxic our state was. People didn’t trust one another. I was not comfortable with how the state was divided along the locations where people lived. People go to work together and eat together as family and friends. But when they close their offices, they go to different places because nobody trusts one another. I felt Kaduna State was the most important city in all of Northern Nigeria. At that time, I believed the only thing we needed to do was restore the glory of our state. Today, I’m happy. Gradually, we are restoring the glory of our state. Everyone now feels comfortable. Everyone wants to stay in Kaduna. That was the reason why, when the president wanted to launch his campaign, he chose Kaduna. The Kaduna of the past is different from the Kaduna of today. Everyone feels Kaduna is home now. We quickly abolished the issue of citizen and indigene dichotomy because our strength is in our diversity. But most importantly, we are highly cosmopolitan. That is the reason we don’t look at things through the lenses of religion, geography, or ethnicity. After three and a half years, have you achieved the Kaduna of your dream? Yes, I can say that largely. But I still believe we can do more, simply because we cannot rest. We must consolidate. When I say merchants, the merchants are not going to give up. I’m not sure we have completely defeated them. We have done a lot. If we rest, they will take us back. I remember when we were trying to choose our deputy governor; a lot of people thought it was difficult. But I said, no, this is a new Kaduna. Nobody will worry about whether it is a Muslim or a Christian. We have moved beyond that. When we decided to make a decision, people thought there would be issues. Nobody said a word. In three years, we have done a lot to promote interfaith harmony in our state. All the leaders of both religions who didn’t sit at the same table now sit together. They understand poverty has no ethnic or tribal mark. It has no respect for religion or ethnicity. The poor man is a poor man. The only thing is that they believe we need to work together. They put that aside and now think about how to move us forward. Because at the end of the day, the elites still live together. It’s only the poor people who are separated. Who is really working to ensure the poor people remain separated? It is the elites. It was an easy decision to say, look, the elites cannot live together while the poor people live separately. You cannot do that. I will not accept that. When I came in, in the first month, I was giving people a lot of land. There were some I gave land to in a particular place. They sold it because they said they could not live in such a place. Today, I’m working to ensure that everyone lives together. Just lik

item.title: OPEC+ holds December oil output steady to support market stability
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, known as OPEC+, have agreed to maintain their September 2026 required production levels for December to support stability in the global oil market. The countries — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — reached the agreement at a virtual meeting on November 1, 2026, where they reviewed “global market conditions and outlook”. The seven producers, which announced additional voluntary production adjustments in April and November 2023, decided to retain their existing production requirements for December. In a statement after the meeting, the countries reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation among oil-producing nations and stability in the international market. The statement read: “The seven participating countries decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026.” The countries also reiterated their “collective commitment to achieve full conformity with the Declaration of Cooperation”, the framework guiding collaboration between OPEC members and participating non-OPEC oil producers. They added that they would continue to monitor developments in the global oil market through regular consultations. “The seven OPEC+ countries will continue to hold monthly meetings to review market conditions. The next meeting will be held on 29 November 2026,” the statement said. The seven countries’ combined required production level for December stands at 31.01 million barrels per day (bpd), according to the accompanying production schedule. Saudi Arabia has the highest required production level at 10.478 million bpd, followed by Russia with 9.949 million bpd and Iraq with 4.431 million bpd. Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman have required production levels of 2.676 million bpd, 1.628 million bpd, 1.007 million bpd and 841,000 bpd, respectively. Reacting to the development in an interview, an energy analyst, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the decision could support international crude oil prices, with positive implications for Nigeria’s revenue and foreign exchange earnings. The post OPEC+ holds December oil output steady to support market stability appeared first on Vanguard News .

Dickson, who spoke in a statement following his homecoming to Bayelsa, weekend, which witnessed the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat, said the governor’s decision to join the APC amounted to ‘donating’ the state to a party he claimed had never won Bayelsa through the ballot. He, however, declared that the time had come to make his political position clear, accusing Diri of abandoning the political structure that nurtured and supported his emergence as governor. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Samuel Oyadongha Yenagoa—Former Bayelsa State Governor, Seriake Dickson, has accused his successor, Governor Douye Diri, of surrendering government they built together to a party that never won the state through the ballot. Dickson, who spoke in a statement following his homecoming to Bayelsa, weekend, which witnessed the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat, said the governor’s decision to join the APC amounted to ‘donating’ the state to a party he claimed had never won Bayelsa through the ballot. The National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) said he had deliberately refrained from commenting extensively on developments in the state to avoid creating political tension and preserve peace. He, however, declared that the time had come to make his political position clear, accusing Diri of abandoning the political structure that nurtured and supported his emergence as governor. He said: “Every single one of the people in the current government was nurtured and supported for years by me.” The former governor recalled that Diri served as his Executive Secretary, Deputy Chief of Staff, member of the House of Representatives and Senator before succeeding him as governor. Dickson said his decision to support Diri’s emergence was informed by the need to sustain Ijaw political leadership and promote fairness among the different local government areas in Bayelsa. He alleged that his successor had now turned against those who supported his political journey, accusing the administration of pettiness, propaganda, blackmail and victimisation. “Our victory was donated free of charge to the APC, making all of us overnight opposition members in our own state, in a government we formed, in a governorship I crafted, and an administration we worked hard to put in power,” he said. Dickson maintained that the APC had never defeated him or won Bayelsa State at the polls, claiming that his political influence had prevented the party from taking control of the state since 2015. He expressed disappointment that Diri had aligned with the APC without securing what he described as corresponding benefits for Bayelsa from the Federal Government. The senator also criticised the Federal Government over what he described as inadequate infrastructure development and insufficient representation of Bayelsa and the Niger Delta in federal appointments. He, however, urged his supporters to remain peaceful and avoid personal attacks against the governor. “As I said, children may deny their father, but fathers do not deny children. The governor is still my person, my brother, my compatriot and our governor. But he is now someone I disagree with, as he and the people in his government are wrong with the direction they are taking our state to,” he said. Diri won’t respond — Aide An aide to Governor Diri, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the governor would not respond to Dickson’s allegations. “The governor doesn’t want to respond to him. That’s just the truth. Everybody is free to say whatever they want to say. We decided we don’t want to make any issue out of it. We are focused on what we want to do for Bayelsans. Let Bayelsans be the judge. That’s all we care about,” the aide said. Miriki faults Dickson’s remarks Technical Adviser to the Bayelsa State Governor on General Duties, Miriki Ebikibina, described Dickson’s comment as unfortunate, urging the former governor to exercise restraint and uphold the dignity expected of a former chief executive of the state and a serving senator. He questioned the propriety of Senator Dickson’s remarks, considering the political support and opportunities he received from former President Goodluck Jonathan, including his appointments as a commissioner and Attorney-General, as well as his emergence as a member of the House of Representatives and later as governor of Bayelsa State. Ebikibina also recalled the political circumstances surrounding Dickson’s emergence as the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, claiming that party stakeholders, including former President Jonathan and King A.J. Turner, played significant roles in securing his candidacy and electoral victory. He called on Senator Dickson and the NDC to emulate the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, whom he described as having focused his campaign on issues rather than personal attacks. According to Ebikibina, “the Diri administration’s achievements reflect purposeful leadership and effective governance. Political disagreements should not overshadow constructive engagement on issues affecting the state.” Obi to Tinubu: You’re tired, quit 2027 race Meanwhile, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ,NDC, Peter Obi, has asked President Bola Tinubu to abandon his re-election bid in 2027, declaring that Nigeria needs a leader with the energy and capacity to tackle the country’s worsening economic and security challenges. Obi, who urged Tinubu to retire from the presidential race and return home to rest, said Nigerians could no longer afford leadership that, in his view, lacked the drive to confront the country’s mounting problems. The former Anambra State governor spoke on Friday in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, during the commissioning of the NDC campaign office and secretariat. He accused the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government of failing to address widespread poverty, hunger, unemployment, insecurity, poor healthcare and inadequate electricity supply. He said millions of Nigerians could no longer afford basic necessities, while access to quality healthcare, education and employment remained a major challenge. Taking a direct swipe at Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Obi said, “The man is tired. He needs to go home. Tinubu must go and rest. We want him to go and rest. “Today, we have a country that produces the highest number of poor people in the world. Today, we have a country where our people are hungry. Nigerians don’t know where the next meal will come from.” He lamented that the collapse of public healthcare had forced some Nigerians to resort to spiritual interventions instead of seeking medical attention, while poor educational infrastructure and unemployment continued to undermine the country’s development. Outlining his party’s agenda, Obi said an NDC government would prioritise national unity, security, domestic production, accountability and job creation. “We are telling you that NDC is coming to build a new Nigeria that is possible. We want to move Nigeria from consumption to production. We will start by uniting the country,” he said. He pledged to strengthen public institutions, tackle insecurity and guarantee equal opportunities for Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic or geographical backgrounds. item.title: 3 feared dead, 5 rescued as two-storey building collapses in Osun
item.description: By Shina Abubakar OSOGBO—THREE persons have been confirmed dead and five rescued alive after a two-storey commercial building under construction collapsed at Owode-Ede, in Ede North Local Government Area of Osun State. The incident occurred at Zone 8, Oke Alaafia Community, at about 11pm on Friday, prompting a rescue operation by the Federal Fire Service and other emergency responders. In a statement, the spokesperson for the Federal Fire Service, Osun State Command, DSF Ojo Omoyemi Olamide, said the command received a distress call through its emergency line at about 11:30pm and immediately mobilised personnel to the scene. She said the five rescued victims were taken to Idera Specialist Hospital, Ede, for urgent medical attention, while the three bodies recovered were handed over to the Nigeria Police Force, A Division, Ede. “The incident involved a two-storey shopping complex used for commercial purposes. The building consists of six shops on the upper floor, six shops on the middle floor and two stores on the ground floor, covering an area of about 50m by 100m. “Preliminary investigation reveals that structural defects and the use of substandard materials are suspected to be the cause of the collapse,” she stated. Olamide said the rescue operation was completed and personnel returned to the station at about 9:26am on Saturday. She added that the estimated property loss was N100 million, while property worth approximately N150 million was saved. The operation was conducted in collaboration with the Osun State Fire Service, Ede Station; the Nigeria Police Force, A Division, Ede; and personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Owode-Ede Division. item.title: Gunmen abduct Plateau varsity student, shoot another in Bokkos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS—GUNMEN suspected to be kidnappers have abducted a 100-level female student of Plateau State University (PLASU), Bokkos, and shot another person during an attack on an off-campus student residential area in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incidents occurred on Saturday at about 8:40pm, raising concerns over the safety of students living outside the university campus. A student, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed the abduction to journalists in Jos on Sunday, saying the victim had gone out with another female student when she was seized. “Yes, the student was taken away by the attackers last night, and we have not seen her since then. She lives off-campus, but I don’t know her personally,” the student said. He lamented the growing insecurity in the area and appealed to security agencies to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted student. A university staff member, who also spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to comment publicly, said the institution was aware of the incident. “The university is aware of a reported shooting incident in one of the off-campus student residential areas. This would be the second such incident in four weeks,” he said. “While the incident did not occur within the university campus, which remains our direct responsibility to secure, we are deeply concerned that any of our students living off-campus should face such threats to their safety,” he added. The staff member said the administration of Prof. Shadrack Best had made concerted efforts to provide safe on-campus accommodation for all students. “However, due to severe financial constraints, the university is currently only able to accommodate about 1,000 students in its dormitories,” he stated. “The university appreciates the support of its Visitor and Plateau State Governor, Barr. Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, as well as the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, TETFund, for providing critical infrastructure at the institution,” he said. “The university will continue to engage relevant authorities to expand both accommodation and security for our nearly 20,000 students,” he added. Efforts to reach the Plateau State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Alfred Alabo, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen abduct Plateau varsity student, shoot another in Bokkos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 2 – A Long Cloud on Mars
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 2 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Long Cloud on Mars Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth . Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth . item.title: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable. But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector. Read Also: NAFDAC secures five-year jail term for fake Goya oil manufacturer Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags. The cost of a crunch The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal. The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years. For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating. “If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away. “People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.” The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil. As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell. Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks. A lifestyle of hustle and denial In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation. The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary. With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred. Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product. “The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch. “I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.” For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly. Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health. The regulatory blindspot Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives. However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible. Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable. Public health

item.title: Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 25, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison North-central Pennsylvania is canyon country with an Appalachian flair. Pine Creek Gorge reaches depths of about 1,500 feet (460 meters) along its gently curving path through the forests of the Allegheny Plateau . Instead of the steep rock walls characteristic of canyons in the desert Southwest, lushly vegetated slopes outline the dramatic topography. In autumn, greens give way to a palette of reds and golds sought out by leaf peepers. Nicknamed the “Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania,” the gorge runs for some 45 miles (72 kilometers) from Ansonia south to Pine Creek’s confluence with the West Branch Susquehanna River, reaching its greatest depths around Waterville. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite captured this image of Pine Creek Gorge on October 25, 2026, when colorful fall foliage was on display. Glaciers played a key role in the canyon’s formation, though ice itself did not carve it. Pine Creek once flowed to the north , opposite of what it does today. As glaciers advanced into the region from the northeast during the last ice age, they dammed the river and filled the valley with lakes. Those lakes eventually overflowed, sending water streaming to the south. Autumn colors emerge along Pine Creek Gorge in this view from Colton Point State Park on October 11, 2009. fishhawk , via Flickr When the ice receded, Pine Creek was already becoming entrenched in its southward course. Rocks and sand left behind by the melting ice further prevented the water from turning back north. Glacial meltwater continued to rush through the valley, deepening and shaping it into its current form. Today, the hillsides around the gorge are blanketed in northern hardwood and mixed oak forest, sprinkled with hemlock and white pine. In autumn, the deciduous trees impart red and gold hues to the landscape akin to the rock of the famous Arizona canyon . Those lakes eventually overflowed, sending water streaming to the south. October 9 October 25 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 9 October 25 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 9 October 25 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Image Details Foliage in the northern hardwood and oak forests around Pennsylvania’s Pine Creek Gorge takes on fall color between October 9, 2026 (left), and October 25, 2026 (right). The images were acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 . NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison. This seasonal change around Pine Creek Gorge has not always been so visually pleasing. With increasing demand for wood products in early 19th-century America, loggers found their way to the area’s stately trees. At the time, white pine and hemlock several feet in diameter and towering hardwoods populated the slopes around Pine Creek Gorge. The pines were especially valued for making ship masts, and hemlock bark was used to tan leather. Before railroads, logs were floated down Pine Creek to the Susquehanna in massive drives. By the early 20th century, decades of logging left the land so barren that the area earned the moniker “Pennsylvania Desert.” The forest has since returned, and with it, wild inhabitants such as black bears, coyotes, bobcats, timber rattlesnakes, and a diversity of songbirds. In 1968, an area of 30,000 acres (12,000 hectares) was designated a National Natural Landmark . Visitors can experience the gorge’s natural splendor at many points along its path, including from multiple state parks and the Pine Creek Rail Trail . item.title: Luke Skywalker's Single Greatest Star Wars Line Hits Harder Than Any Sci-Fi Quote Since
item.description: Since its 2018 debut, Rian Johnson’s The Last Jedi has sparked heated debate over whether it was a fantastic or terrible Star Wars film for Luke Skywalker. Still, whatever your opinion, it’s hard to deny that Johnson’s take on the greatest Jedi ever came with some truly epic quotes. And no, we’re not talking about the zinger, “Amazing. Every word of what you just said was wrong.”
